When Saturn Risin9 auditioned for Jordan Firstman’s “ Club Kid ,” her face was still swollen from facial feminization surgery. The musician, DJ and nightlife fixture, who had undergone the procedure a month earlier in April 2025, hadn't even attempted to put on a wig since her surgery. Unable to bring herself to let anyone into her apartment, she played all three characters in her self-tape.

“I think they were just like, ‘Who is this crazy lady?’” Risin9 recalls with a laugh. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Samantha Morton to Receive BFI Fellowship

Firstman, a longtime friend from the nightlife circuit, had told Risin9 at a party two years earlier that he was writing a role for her. But the audition request came just weeks after her gender-affirming surgery. For Risin9, the timing felt like an affirmation — "I thought it was so aligned, at the moment that I was so authentic with myself, that the world opened up to me," she says.

Now, Risin9 is one of the breakout stars of Firstman's A24 comedy-drama, which follows a New York City party promoter whose life is upended by the arrival of a son he never knew he had. As Saffron, a DJ with a protective streak and diva sensibilities, Risin9 brings to the film two decades of experience navigating underground nightlife.

The Bay Area native grew up performing in theater productions and wrote her first play at 11, but turned her attention to music in her 20s after finding that the acting roles available to her didn't align with her identity. She built a career as an independent recording artist, DJ and performer, touring internationally before relocating to Los Angeles in 2017. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Perhaps most gratifying to Risin9 has been the film's reception among audiences far removed from the world it depicts. After a screening at Telluride Film Festival, she was approached by a father who was crying in the arms of his daughter. "I was like, 'Are you okay?,'" she recalls. "And he was like, 'Your movie was just so beautiful.'"

Even Risin9's mother, who has historically been less comfortable watching queer intimacy on screen, ("She likes to pretend that she can't watch people make out and I'm like, 'I think you just don't want to see gay stuff') came away a fan.

The film's success also comes at a particularly exciting moment for queer cinema. In addition to "Club Kid," stories centered on gay men — such as "Elsinore," "La Bola Negra" and "Artificial" — dominate awards season buzz this year. "These films exist in a post-'Heated Rivalry' moment during which audiences seem newly open to queer stories," Variety's Dan D'Addario wrote last month, posing the question: is this the gayest Oscar season ever? "These films launch into surprising directions, showing many different sides of the gay experience."

Risin9 similarly describes this era as the "de-'Will & Grace’-ification of queer art,” in which LGBTQ stories are increasingly afforded the complexity, specificity and messiness that Hollywood has long granted their heterosexual counterparts. "Straight people want to see more things that they don't know about," she says. "We all want to learn. We don't want to stagnate."

Below, Risin9 talks about her audition process, her evolving relationship with nightlife and teaching her young co-star Reggie Absolom to DJ:

Léa Seydoux told me that she loved me in “Club Kid.” She just comes up to me and goes “I love you in the movie,” and I was like, “You saw ‘Club Kid’?” She was like, “I loved it,” and we actually walked the red carpet for “Gentle Monster” in Cannes. So it was kind of a kismet moment.

She had that knowingness that she was giving me something. You know what I mean? Like, “I have to tell you this, and you're gonna live for it.” It was so cute.

I didn't want to be too aware of what was happening because something that I love about acting is letting go and finding that space where you know the rhythm of it and you know what your cues are, but you're also allowing for the character to be thinking and to be human instead of just waiting to perform. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The first scene that we shot was the one where we go to Peter’s [Firstman's] house and find out that he has Arlo, and we're all busting in the house. I was supposed to say a few words about convincing him to do this party — and I was saying it so big, and Jordan just goes, "Just say it.” And I was like, “Oh, okay.”

That was what Jordan's direction always was. It was a lot of trust, but also the encouragement to be comfortable in it and not to be so showy.

Jordan and I were very friendly party friends. We've always had a really good rapport, and we hung out once in Atlanta. I brought my little cousin with me and I'm very protective of my family. I'm the disciplinarian. So I think he got to see that outside of the "most fun girl at the party," I’m also this maternal, super supportive figure. And I think his wheels started to turn.

I saw him about two years later at a party, and he was like, “Hey, I wrote this movie and I wrote a role for you. Would you be in my movie?” It's like 5 a.m. So I'm like, “Yeah, girl, whatever.” You know how many people stop me at the end of the night and say, “Oh my God, it would be so cool if we did this?”

I showed up in a fully laced bodysuit, thinking that they wanted to see a club diva. So I'm in this lace bodysuit at 10 a.m. in Hollywood. And I thought they wanted one of those nasty girls. I was reading it kind of cunty.

And then at the end, Carmen Cuba, our casting director, was like, “Can you do it more empathetic?” And I was like, “Okay, that's me! Let's talk. Let's go.”

There's a line in the movie where it's like, “When's the last time you saw a kid?” And I was like, really, actually, when was the last time I saw a kid? Because I also didn't know if he knew trans people. I was in my head. The last time I saw a kid, the kid was bullying me. So I was like, “Whoa!” Kids can be scary. And he could be a bro who just randomly got cast in this queer movie.

So I was just so surprised at how well-adjusted and kind and really cool he is. We were going over these vinyl and I'm like, “Do you like this one?” He's like, “No, I like heavy metal.” And I was like, “Oh!” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I really did teach him how to DJ because Twitter is a scary place, and I'd hate for someone to zoom in on the movie and be like, "Why are you turning those knobs?" Now we’ve done DJ sets together and he actually knows what he's doing.

I think this might be the first year where I'm not seeing the shortcomings. I'm seeing incredibly different stories. I love that "Club Kid” is like the de-"Will & Grace”-ification of queer art because that was that safety that they were selling in the '90s and it kind of kept going for so long. Like, “Oh, we're just kind of quirky, normal people who like to shop,” or something. And it's just so much realer than that.

And even “La Bola Negra” being this Odyssey-level film. It's incredible that there are so many different avenues of our lives and our fantasies being shown in the way that everything else is shown in the world because it's normal. Life is normal for the people that are living it, and many people live many different lives.

  Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google LEGO Black Friday deals are live, and there are so many delightful things to see that it truly feels like Christmas morning for LEGO fans. From the launch of Godzilla to all the gifts you can get with your purchases, not to mention the opportunity for LEGO Insiders to earn 4X points, there are so many deals to take advantage of.

LEGO's Black Friday sale kicks off November 27 and runs through November 30, and you can earn three gifts during the sale. The first is the Godzilla Logo and Footprint (40888), an exclusive gift that comes with the purchase of Godzilla . Featuring 359 pieces, measuring 3.5 inches high, 9.5 inches wide, and 5 inches deep, and intended for builders 18 and up, this set is a perfect complement to the mighty kaiju. The footprint matches Godzilla's foot exactly, and the bright blue letters have a Hollywood feel.

The second gift with purchase is the Retro Jukebox (40914), which you get when you spend $250 or more. It has 287 pieces, measures 5.5 inches high, 3 inches wide, and 2 inches deep, and is intended for builders aged 18 and up. The jukebox features a record that spins, and it opens to reveal a smaller jukebox and a minifigure.

The last gift with purchase is the Winter Snow Globe (40918), which you'll get free when you spend $170 or more. This delightful holiday build contains 231 pieces, measures 3.5 inches high, 4 inches wide, and 4 inches deep, and is intended for builders 10 years old and up. Featuring a Christmas tree that spins, a snowman with a hat and scarf, and presents, it's a charming addition to any LEGO collection.

Speaking of Godzilla , the iconic movie monster makes its big debut today on LEGO.com. Godzilla's stature is appropriately huge at over 27.5 inches tall (with heat ray) and features 5,363 pieces, making this an advanced build for those 18 years old and up. With an attachable tongue and heat ray, you can pose this fearsome beast's arms, fingers, tail, and head to capture its most memorable on-screen moments.

Several Star Wars LEGO sets on sale will be retired at the end of the year, so there's no better time to add them to your collection. We have a complete list of all of the Star Wars sets being retired on December 31 you can check out.

Along with the Star Wars sets on sale, there's also a collectible book, several plushes, and a few keychains on sale worth checking out.

Amazon has a lot of deals on Star Wars sets that LEGO.com does not, so make sure you swing by to check these out if you're trying to fill out your Star Wars LEGO collection. Some of them are at the lowest prices we've ever seen them at, or the lowest price in 90 days, like the SMART Play: Luke's Landspeeder set.

The LEGO Black Friday deals have quite a few sets below $50, making them ideal for gift-giving. These are our top picks in that price range.

When does Black Friday start and end? LEGO's Black Friday sale starts on November 27, 2026, and "Black Friday Weekend" ends on Cyber Monday, November 30. LEGO says its offers last through the weekend while stocks last. Popular sets and free gifts can sell out early, so it's best to shop sooner.

Is LEGO cheaper on Black Friday?

Often, yes, but where you shop makes a difference. LEGO.com focuses on exclusives and free gifts, while stores like Amazon usually have bigger price cuts. Amazon started early LEGO Black Friday deals with up to 50% off select sets.

Do I need to be a LEGO Insider to get Black Friday deals?

You don't need to be a member to shop the sale, but joining is worth it. LEGO Insiders is free to join, and members earn points on every purchase that they can spend on members-only rewards, discounts and gifts. You'll need an account to earn points on your Black Friday order.

Where can I find the best LEGO Black Friday deals?

For gifts and new launches like Godzilla, shop LEGO.com or a LEGO Store. For the biggest discounts on existing sets, check Amazon, Walmart, and Target, which often drop LEGO prices further than LEGO does. We'll keep this page updated with the best prices we find through Cyber Monday.

articles.title: How The Family Of Breaking Bad’s RJ Mitte Paid Tribute To The Late Actor On Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Mitte's family continue to mourn the actor.
articles.content:
The holidays are a great time to be around family and celebrate their company, but they are always more difficult when you’ve just lost a loved one. Breaking Bad cast member RJ Mitte died on October 12, 2026, at the age of 34 by suicide. The loss is still fresh for his mother and sister, and they took some time to publicly pay tribute to him on Thanksgiving.

Mitte’s mom shared a photo of herself with RJ Mitte and his sister Lacianne Carriere. She wrote that she’s “missing” him on Thanksgiving, but she “made all [his] favorites”. RJ’s sister also took to her Instagram account to share a throwback photo with the late actor. Here it is:

RJ’s younger sister expressed that she’s “thankful for the time” she had with her brother, and is really feeling his absence on the first holiday she and her family are spending without him. About a month ago, Carriere took to the platform to share a long tribute to RJ, calling him her “everything” and “other half”. It’s a particularly huge loss for his closest relatives.

Mitte’s body was found by his mother on the morning of October 12 in his home in Brownville, Texas. His official cause of death was ruled a suicide the same day. His mother said she had offered and suggested her son go to therapy in the three months before his passing, but he said he was “OK” and “handling it” (via Today ).

articles.summary: After the loss of Patrick Stewart this October, Kevin Feige has shared an anecdote about the late star on the set of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness—and it involves some Star Trek spoilers. Marvel fans, Star Trek fans, and innumerable fans of Patrick Stewart's work in general were devastated last month when it […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google After the loss of Patrick Stewart this October, Kevin Feige has shared an anecdote about the late star on the set of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness —and it involves some Star Trek spoilers. Marvel fans, Star Trek fans, and innumerable fans of Patrick Stewart's work in general were devastated last month when it was confirmed that Stewart had passed. This also means that his role as Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday will be the storied actor's final on-screen appearance , making it all the more significant and notable. That wasn't Stewart's first appearance in the MCU, though. That occurred several years ago, in Multiverse of Madness .

As audiences anxiously await the arrival of Doomsday in just a few weeks, which will finally offer fans that look at Stewart's last performance, Feige has provided a hilarious anecdote from on the set of Multiverse of Madness in an interview with Entertainment Weekly . Apparently, while filming that movie, Feige, who is a self-proclaimed Trekkie, didn't even have to poke Stewart a bit for some answers regarding the TV series Star Trek: Picard . While one might suspect that Stewart would keep any such details tightly under wraps, Feige found that was far from the case. Check out Feige's exact comments below.

Speaking to Entertainment Weekly about his time on set with Stewart, Feige shared that he didn't even have to push for Picard spoilers, saying, "He volunteered a few, and then I told him to stop. I just wanted to watch and enjoy the show." It's funny to imagine this dynamic, in which Stewart is readily offering up spoilers for the show, so much so that Feige has to stop him because he's genuinely enjoying the series, but it also suggests a friendliness between Stewart and Feige on set that is nice to imagine, especially considering that they reunited for Doomsday .

It will also be interesting to see how Stewart's role in Doomsday is different from that of Multiverse of Madness —especially because many fans are hoping to see quite a bit more power from Charles Xavier in Doomsday , following his death in Multiverse of Madness , in which the Scarlet Witch snapped his neck. Granted, that was meant to showcase just how powerful Wanda was at that point, and it did so, but X-Men fans were still largely disappointed with this fate and wanted to see more from Professor X. Presumably, they finally will with Doomsday , and hopefully, that will be a proper send off for the star who absolutely deserves some major moments of heroism in the upcoming movie. Either way, though, it will be very sad to see the movie conclude and know that this iconic actor is no longer with us.

What do you hope to see from Charles Xavier in Doomsday ? Let us know in the comments down below.

articles.title: Federal Incentive Will Level The Playing Field For America's Creatives — Guest Column
articles.summary: Editor's note: Ruth Vitale, who previously held top posts at Paramount Classics, Fine Line Features and New Line Cinema, is CEO of CreativeFuture, a nonprofit coalition of more than 500 companies and organizations and nearly 300,000 individuals devoted to promoting the value of creativity in the digital age. For more than a decade, CreativeFuture has […]

Editor's note: Ruth Vitale , who previously held top posts at Paramount Classics, Fine Line Features and New Line Cinema, is CEO of CreativeFuture , a nonprofit coalition of more than 500 companies and organizations and nearly 300,000 individuals devoted to promoting the value of creativity in the digital age.

For more than a decade, CreativeFuture has fought for one simple idea: Members of our creative communities deserve to make a living from the work they create. We have taken on piracy. We have taken on Big Tech. We have taken on criminal enterprises that profit from the theft of our movies, television, music, and books. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Trump's "Noisy Name-Calling" Mocked By NYT After Bored POTUS Starts Thanksgiving Ranting Against Reporter's Nvidia Dispatch News Jane Fonda, Robert De Niro & Other Figures Sign Letter Backing Chris Van Hollen For Majority Leader --- Amid A Chuck Schumer Aide's Prank

But right now, America’s creative community faces a different kind of threat. Fewer movies and television shows are being produced in this country. Copyright protects creative work once it exists. It does nothing for the American crews who never got the opportunity to make it. I have spent my entire career in this business – at Vestron, where we made Dirty Dancing , and then at United Artists, Fine Line Features, and Paramount Classics, where we released films like Child’s Play , Road House, Shine, You Can Count on Me, and Hustle & Flow. I have watched independent filmmakers scrape together budgets one dollar at a time. Today, I hear the same question from filmmakers repeatedly: Can we afford to make this in America?

More and more often, the answer is no.

At least 65 countries now offer national production incentives, sometimes in addition to local or regional ones. The United States does not. Thirty-nine states have built programs of their own, but a state program cannot outbid a government overseas with more competitive incentives in place, and the numbers show it. America’s share of global film production has fallen from 52% in 2022, to just 38% at the start of 2026. The share was 65% just over a decade ago.

Let’s be clear about who pays the price. Film and television support more than two million American jobs and pay over $200 billion in wages a year. Nationally, the industry supports 162,000 businesses, 93% of which employ fewer than 10 people. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Those paychecks go to editors and composers, costume designers and carpenters, camera operators and writers’ assistants. Many of them work from project to project, with no guarantee there will be a next one. When a production moves overseas, their jobs move without them.

That is why I am so encouraged by the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act (MPTERA). Introduced last month with strong bipartisan support in both chambers, it would create federal tax relief for film and television made in America based on the U.S. jobs created, including for postproduction and visual effects. Editing suites and effects houses can be anywhere in the world – which means they can just as easily be somewhere other than here.

MPTERA also gives independent productions extra relief, up to 30% of the amount spent on U.S. jobs. As someone who has built much of my career championing independent film, I can tell you that matters. Independent films are where new voices are discovered, and run on margins so thin that an overseas incentive can decide whether they get shot in Albuquerque or Belfast. Or whether they get shot at all.

The upside is enormous. A new study estimates that a federal incentive would support an average of more than 143,000 jobs a year and generate nearly $250 billion in additional economic activity over eight years. And this won’t help only California and New York – our industry is in every state of the union, leaving its economic mark everywhere it goes. There is also a bonus for productions in rural areas or for producers that film in at least 10 states in a year. And keep in mind, a feature film’s location shoot generates an average of $670,000 per day for local communities. For a one-hour television episode, it’s $475,000 per day.

Bottom line: This is not a giveaway. Not a single taxpayer dollar goes to the production – the legislation simply reduces the tax liability of U.S. productions. It is a smart investment in one of the few industries where America still leads the world. Our film and television industry maintains a trade surplus with nearly every nation on Earth. When Americans were asked what their country does better than any other, 58% named movies and television as their top answer. Why would we let that slip away?

Other countries have quickly realized the economic benefit that production brings. Standing still here at home is not a policy. It is clearly a forfeit. This is a bill that has the support of President Trump, as well as Senators Tim Scott and Adam Schiff and Reps. Nathaniel Moran and Linda Sánchez, and 90 other members of Congress. This is the rare bill that has reached across the aisle and to the White House. That doesn’t happen often.

Congress should pass MPTERA this year. We already have the talent and resources and will see the benefit immediately. America’s creatives are ready to work. Let’s give them the chance to do it here at home.

articles.title: 5 Superman Moments That Split the Fandom, and We’re Still Arguing About Decades Later
articles.summary: Courtesy of DC Comics There's no character who defines what superheroes look and act like better than Superman. He was the character who codified the genre as a whole and has served as the gold standard for heroics ever since. Superman's adventures have brought about some of the most iconic and defining moments in comic book history, but not […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There's no character who defines what superheroes look and act like better than Superman . He was the character who codified the genre as a whole and has served as the gold standard for heroics ever since. Superman's adventures have brought about some of the most iconic and defining moments in comic book history, but not all of those actions are remembered fondly. The majority of Superman's memorable moments are looked back on with praise and enjoyment, but there are some that are so controversial, so divisive, and so downright polarizing that they still have the fandom picking sides like it's an active war. Today, we're looking at five of those moments, and honing in on exactly what makes them so fraught with conflict.

The ultimate modern example of this phenomenon came about when Jon Kent, then Superboy, was unceremoniously aged from ten to seventeen years old , effectively transforming him into an entirely different character. The vitriol from fans was practically universal. Jon was the most popular and beloved addition to Superman's cast in decades, advancing the Man of Steel's character in a natural and new way. Then came this rug pull just when Jon was reaching incredible heights of popularity. Not only did fans lose out on seeing him develop, but Superman and Lois did too, and that was a tragedy that these heroes should never have had to live through.

The campaign to restore Jon's age was, unfortunately, in vain, as he's still an adult to this day. There are still fans who fight for this reversal, but most people have moved on, choosing instead to follow what DC is doing with Jon now. By this point, he's been an adult longer than he was a kid, so while there's still a vocal minority screaming that Jon needs to return to childhood, it's more become a point of contention amongst fans rather than a unifier. The real reason this fight lasted so long is that DC clearly had no idea what to do with Jon until very, very recently, so I expect this split to heal over time as Jon finally becomes his own character again.

If the previous entry was the perfect example of this split, then this entry is the best minor showcase of it. Back in the '90s, superheroes across the board were replaced or rebranded with edgy new designs and harsh, sleek new directions. Azrael became a murderous Batman who wore armor, and Wonder Woman wore all leather, for crying out loud. Even Superman couldn't escape it, as he found himself transformed into a being of pure energy , his powers totally altered and being forced to use a containment suit. Eventually, it was revealed that he had actually split into two versions of himself. One was red, and one was blue.

To this day, fans can't seem to decide if they hate this redesign or look back on it with some comical nostalgia. This new direction for Superman is the peak of what the '90s sought to do to superheroes, fundamentally altering them in an attempt to update them for a modern new world. This type of thing is always tricky, but it's a hundred times more so with Superman, who is practically the face of the unchanging status quo. Altering an iconic character almost always results in something fans either love or hate, with very little ground in between. This is a great example of that with low stakes, where fans either find this new look a fun change of pace, or an affront to Superman himself.

Supergirl is an iconic, beloved piece of Superman's lore, but her origin hides a piece of his history that nobody seems to know what to do with. After Kara first landed on Earth, Superman decided that her staying with Clark Kent would raise too many questions, and since his parents were dead, Kara wound up living at an orphanage in Midvale. She would stay there for several real-world years, until she let herself be adopted and Supergirl was introduced to the world. However, many fans find it a hard pill to swallow that Superman of all people would leave the only other survivor of both his kind and family in an orphanage, but there's some nuance here.

Fans usually take one of two stances here. One is that this is a moral failing on Clark's part that came from inexperience and that should be brought up to show that he isn't perfect. The other is acknowledging that this was clearly done for the real-world reason of keeping Supergirl a secret and away from Superman's main adventures until the team could gauge fans' reactions. It was literally a proving ground for her character. There have even been plenty of justifications added, from Kara choosing to stay amongst kids her own age to Clark being physically unable to raise her himself. Still, the phrase "Superman left her in an orphanage" is just hard to defend, and really only Mark Waid tries to do so from a writing perspective. Most fans choose to forget about this for many reasons, as it's sure to bring up arguments.

This is something that DC attempts to do every now and again, and the reason it's so divisive is that it makes sense on paper. Superman and Wonder Woman are the faces of superheroes and superheroines, respectively, and also stand head and shoulders above the rest in terms of raw strength and abilities. They've always had a very strong relationship, although it has almost always been portrayed as platonic aside from when DC pushes the boundaries. They clearly love each other deeply, being close as few other heroes are, and are always compared when they come up, so it truly does make sense on paper, but only on paper, not on panel.

The reason that this remains so controversial is twofold. One is that both Clark and Diana have well-established relationships that stretch back to the beginning of their comics, and going against those often makes their new relationships feel temporary or done in spite of the standard. The second reason is that it's rarely written well. Superman and Wonder Woman usually only end up together when parts of their characters are filed off or changed in some way, leading to what comes across as a boring pairing that exists because people think it should, not because they like it. This pairing definitely has its supporters, however, who are sure to fight for its place in history.

Without a doubt, the most controversial moment in Superman's long history so far is when he chose to execute the three pocket dimension versions of General Zod and his cronies. They laid waste to their version of Earth , and even after permanently robbing them of their powers, Superman felt their risk to his home was too great, and he killed them with Kryptonite poisoning. This single moment has split the fandom like nothing else has, as nobody can seem to agree whether this was a tragic, heavy moment or one of the biggest character assassinations of all time.

Superman himself heavily regretted his actions, the stress of which caused him to create an alternate personality who acted out in his sleep, which caused him to exile himself from Earth for some time. However, while the comics have swept this far under the rug, fans still dig up this moment as the central point of argument for whether Superman refuses to kill or is willing to if there is no other choice. This moment is truly emblematic of John Byrne's entire run on Superman, as his Superman would definitely act like this, but fans still must argue whether that version of the character is the agreed-upon standard, or a relic of a time long past.

Which Superman controversy do you think has split fans the most? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google MCU fans have waited five years for concrete movement on a sequel to Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings , currently just being called Shang-Chi 2 , and now, Shang-Chi actor Simu Liu has provided a bit more insight. There has been plenty of frustration over the slow to nonexistent progress on Shang-Chi 2 . Shang-Chi is a legitimately great Marvel movie that arguably didn't get the attention and fanfare it deserved, and it certainly warranted a sequel, especially given the post-credits scenes revealing that Shang-Chi and Katy were recruited for something by Wong and Shang-Chi's sister, Xialing, is now running the Ten Rings.

Liu has also commented on this gap in time before, and he's made it clear that he is very interested in doing another. With those stars aligning, it has been shocking that Shang-Chi 2 hasn't come together more quickly. However, there has been some hope of late, with screenwriter Dave Callaham recently confirming a script is in development . Now, on the heels of that confirmation and less than a month before Avengers: Doomsday finally hits theaters, Liu has given audiences a bit of an update—hopefully, this will be the beginning of more concrete conversations about what is happening with Shang-Chi 2 . Check out Liu's comments below.

Speaking with Entertainment Weekly , Liu said of Shang-Chi , "We had such an incredible time making the first one. Just to have that movie come out and do the numbers that it did and find the audience the way that it did in a time in the world where you couldn’t even buy adjacent seats at the movie theater [amid the COVID-19 pandemic] was really, really incredible." Regarding a potential sequel, Liu added, "I think there was always a conversation that was happening, and I was always super enthusiastic. Seven years ago, I bought a ticket to see Endgame in the theater as a fan and nothing to do with Marvel, didn’t even know that there was a movie on the horizon."

Although there was "always a conversation" surrounding Shang-Chi 2 , the movie seemingly hasn't moved beyond the earliest stages of development and script writing. Instead, Liu has been working on his upcoming appearance in Doomsday . About that project, Liu shared, "To have a scene partner like Channing [Tatum], who is as insistent as I was about getting to do as much of it as possible, was critical to the success of that scene. It was cool to have a dance partner who was as down to get into it as I was. There’s a lot of valid criticisms about the use of CGI in movies and everything, but for what it’s worth, I think we really strived to make that sequence in particular as practical as it possibly could have been."

While audiences don't currently know too much about Doomsday's plot, let alone what Liu's role as Shang-Chi will look like in the movie, this is an exciting update, and it will be interesting to see what the dynamic between Channing Tatum's Gambit and Shang-Chi looks like, especially based on Liu's comments. However, it's Shang-Chi 2 that many fans really want to see.

articles.title: GTA 6 Has Large-Scale Hurricanes, But They Have to First Be Unlocked in a Secret Mission
articles.summary: One of the most impressive aspects of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how Rockstar Games has made Leonida feel like a living, breathing state. And one of the major features that helps with this is the dynamic weather system. Weather can completely transform the experience of GTA 6's open world, especially when it directly impacts […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the most impressive aspects of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how Rockstar Games has made Leonida feel like a living, breathing state. And one of the major features that helps with this is the dynamic weather system. Weather can completely transform the experience of GTA 6's open world, especially when it directly impacts gameplay. Yet, one of the most impactful and thrilling weather conditions is not normally available in the game, but rather must be unlocked first through a secret mission. After completing the mission , players can start to see hurricanes appear naturally in the world.

Considering Leonida is based on Florida, hurricanes are a natural fit for Grand Theft Auto 6 . But they can be devastating, so I see why Rockstar Games locked them behind a mission . The mission itself is found in North Leonard and involves interacting with a doomsday prepper named Freddie. It will take some time and patience to complete the objective, but doing so will not only trigger your first hurricane, but makes them regular occurrences in GTA 6 . These powerful storms can disrupt gameplay in major ways, so consider carefully if you want to go through with this secret unlock.

To unlock hurricanes in GTA 6 , players must travel to a heavily fortified doomsday bunker in North Leonard County. As you approach, you'll be warned through an automated security message, and you will not be able to communicate through the speaker. Instead, you'll have to find your own way in, which begins with heading around the right side of the compound.

You'll spot a yellow bulldozer, which you'll need to use to move the orange shipping container. This reveals an underground entrance where you'll need to follow the sewer system and climb up the ladder at the end. Now you are actually inside the compound, but this is where things get tricky, as multiple landmines are scattered around.

You can either shoot them from a distance or navigate around them using grass and elevated surfaces. Keep your eyes out for a drone and shoot it down using Focus Mode to spot it. Eventually, you'll come to the center where there is a circular bunker, and our doomsday prepper Freddie angrily tells you to leave.

Several in-game days later, you'll receive a message from Freddie who offers to pay you if you can get past his increased security measures. Return to the compound and be prepared to follow a new route; specifically avoid the speaker, as it and your previous route now feature brand new landmines.

Instead, head to the water tower outside the compound and climb onto its first level. From there, jump onto the nearby roof or climb higher to parachute into the compound. Again, you'll need to avoid landmines and destroy any drones that attempt to stop you. Your reward for penetrating Freddie's defenses and interacting with the bunker's entrance is an electrical shock, but afterward Freddie opens the door.

You'll be greeted by Freddie and other inhabitants inside the luxurious and well-stocked bunker. Freddie offers you a drink and a spot on his podcast, but it isn't long before a hurricane warning appears. Freddie then gives you the choice to leave the bunker or stay and wait out the storm. If you decide to leave, you can experience your first GTA 6 hurricane first-hand, though you can do so later if you choose to take shelter.

Completing this encounter permanently introduces random hurricanes into Grand Theft Auto 6 's dynamic weather system. These storms reduce visibility, make driving more difficult, and can damage trees and vulnerable structures. It adds an overall unpredictability to GTA 6 that enhances free-roam, though be prepared just in case a hurricane pops up at the worst time.

articles.title: Star Wars Will Change Genres After 49 Years for New Disney+ TV Series, According to Report
articles.summary: Star Wars may best be known as a space opera epic that straddles the line into fantasy, but it may be dipping its toes into horror very soon. Ever since Disney acquired Lucasfilm and began to release new Star Wars movies and TV shows, the franchise has largely operated within the same confines, even if […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Star Wars may best be known as a space opera epic that straddles the line into fantasy , but it may be dipping its toes into horror very soon. Ever since Disney acquired Lucasfilm and began to release new Star Wars movies and TV shows, the franchise has largely operated within the same confines, even if tonally it works in a few different places. The Mandalorian may be more like a western, Skeleton Crew may be more like an Amblin movie, and Andor is a straight-up political thriller. Now, Star Wars horror is about to go mainstream.

According to insider Daniel Richtman, who teased that Star Wars' television future is still planning a "crossover" event centered around Grand Admiral Thrawn, Lucasfilm is working on a Star Wars horror TV series for Disney+. Fans may recall that the existence of this idea was previously teased by none other than Andor creator Tony Gilroy, who at the time indicated that the Star Wars horror project might be a film . Now it appears to be in development as a show.

Details about the planned Star Wars horror TV series have never been confirmed, not even a hint about who might be writing the script, what era of the franchise it might be taking place in, or what the big monster at the center of it all might be. It's not really a surprise to hear that Lucasfilm is working on it, though, as Disney has actually pushed into the genre in some surprising ways for their streaming platform, including the upcoming Afterlife With Archie TV show that's in the works, plus the reboot of Goosebumps .

In truth, though, Star Wars has changed genres plenty of times over the years; horror is one that it's only toyed with a handful of times. Previously, any time that Star Wars has dabbled in horror it's been almost exclusively within the confines of prose novels. In the '90s, the franchise released a series of books called Galaxy of Fear , following a pair of siblings that ran from undead monsters and mad scientists (offering a Star Wars version of Goosebumps at the time).

Later, Death Troopers by Joe Schreiber introduced zombies into the Star Wars mythology, and plans for another book were revealed earlier this year , called Hiding from the Dark: A Star Wars Horror Novel by horror writer Kiersten White.Suffice to say, there's no shortage of horror ideas waiting for Star Wars to explore, but details remain hidden.

The future of Star Wars is in its most unique position in years now. With the departure of Kathleen Kennedy from Lucasfilm, the company is now being run by Dave Filoni as president & CCO, with Lynwen Brennan as co-president. This past summer's The Mandalorian & Grogu was a commercial flop rejected by audiences, but 2027 is already looking brighter. Not only will the original Star Wars return to theaters, but it will be followed by Star Wars: Starfighter , the first film in the series set after the events of Episode IX .

To date, no grand plan or even a calendar of projects has been revealed to the public about what Star Wars will do next as a series, but reinventing itself with a corner where horror stories can be told feels like a step in the right direction in terms of giving fans something new.

In the trailer for "Tyson Fury," the British boxing champion is seen discussing his mental health struggles, noting that when quizzed by a psychiatrist he "ticked all the boxes … depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder…" Fury's wife then adds that he's a "mild schizophrenic." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Beyoncé Makes Grammys History as First Artist With 100 Nominations Grammy Nominations 2027: Raye Leads With 11 Noms as Rosalía, Olivia Rodrigo, Ella Langley and Other Female Artists Dominate

But now Paris Fury has walked back those claims, putting out a statement denying that her husband has schizophrenia. Netflix has subsequently edited the scene in question out of the documentary.

"I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary," Paris Fury said. Added a Netflix spokesperson: "Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.”

articles.title: Arthur Conti Was Booked This Year With Roles in ‘Carrie’ and ‘Ebenezer.’ Now He’s Looking to Get “a Little Strange”
articles.summary: The 22-year-old has tackled iconic characters in pop culture this year, but he's keeping himself open about what's next.
articles.content:
British actor Arthur Conti is fresh off a whirlwind year. With roles in Mike Flanagan's Carrie adaptation and the recently released Ebenezer , he's been busy crafting new interpretations of well-known characters.

"To play an iconic character that's been played by many people before, and to get to give your own spin on it, is very exciting," Conti tells The Hollywood Reporter over Zoom from London about what he's been up to this year.

The 22-year-old actor is back in the U.K. after over a month of press for Carrie and Ebenezer and a stint in Portland, Oregon. "It's been a bit of a whirlwind, but it's been very enjoyable," he says. After a breakout performance in 2024's Beetlejuice Beetlejuice , 2026 has been the actor's biggest year to date between the two projects and a role in Jane Schoenbrun's Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Why Mike Flanagan Just Couldn't Kill Carrie White Movies 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Slays $120M at Box Office as Franchise Heats Back Up

With Carrie , Conti stepped into the role of teen bully Billy Nolan, first played on screen by John Travolta in Brian De Palma's 1976 film. Conti had read Stephen King's novel but hadn't seen De Palma's film, which he stayed away from during filming. Conti's Billy, while still one of the villains of the story, is different from Travolta's take on the character. "I was worried that even inadvertently or subconsciously I would copy things about that performance, and I really wanted it to be all my own," he says.

Ebenezer finds Conti stepping into the shoes of the titular character of Ebenezer Scrooge — well, the younger version of him anyway. The actor heard that Ti West would be making the film, and as a big fan, he sent in a self-tape. Much like with Carrie , he tried not to take too much inspiration from previous versions of the story, but there's one adaptation that stands out. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"[ The Muppets version] is probably the best one. I mean, it's amazing, that film. Michael Caine gives such a genuinely brilliant, dramatic performance in that film against the Muppets," he says. "He takes it so seriously, and that is the beauty of that film is that you'd think he was talking to John Gielgud, and he's talking to Fozzy."

Despite The Muppets Christmas Carol being his main experience with the story beforehand, he did watch the 1951 film adaptation starring Alastair Sim as Scrooge. "I really liked," he notes.

Below, the actor digs into his last year in roles, what he's looking to do next and how he'd spend a perfect day in London.

I'm always curious, as someone who enjoys it — have you seen Carrie: The Musical ?

We watched it. We saw a theater production on Granville Island in Vancouver. It was a youth theater production of Carrie: The Musical . [The cast of Carrie ] all went to go and see it. Mike [Flanagan] actually put the cast of that production of Carrie in the show. They're all at the prom. Throughout the show, they're in the background at the school, which was really, really fun.

How has the year been? You were busy with Carrie and now Ebenezer .

[ Carrie ] was my first big press tour. It was my first time doing a press junket and all of these things. It feels like the biggest thing that I've done so far [with] how much I've been promoting it. It was all incredibly exciting. [In Carrie ,] I'm playing another character that has several sides to him, after [I did in] Beetlejuice. It's another deceptively charming, manipulative character, which is interesting that I keep taking. ( Laughs ). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Where do you think that's coming from?

Something about me, I don't know. Something untrustworthy. Honestly, it is a treat to play characters like that because you get the chance to do multiple things at once, present a character that has many layers and is complex and isn't wholly one thing or another. It was a great role. It was a really meaty role to sink my teeth into, and it was an honor to play a character of that literary significance. It was a privilege to be entrusted with that.

As an actor, are you drawn to characters that are different from you, then?

It's nice to get outside of yourself — that's part of the fun of it. Growing up, the films I was watching, I was a lot more drawn to flawed or strange or darker characters. I grew up watching Steve Buchemi in Fargo and Philip Seymour Hoffman in Punch-Drunk Love and Talented Mr. Ripley . Those are the kind of characters that I always really loved to watch.

The scope of the projects you had this year has been quite large. Are you drawn to that or looking to change it?

You're right. They are quite large-scale. I think I'm drawn to things that are a little out there and a little strange. Horror is one of the best genres to explore that area because it emboldens filmmakers to experiment and take risks and be a bit weird and a bit dreamlike. That's why I gravitate towards horror a lot, and it's probably what I watch the most of in the cinema.

Is that where you got your love for it? Were you big into horror as a kid? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I think so. It's not horror, just things that are a little strange. My mom brought me up on Charlie Kaufman films. Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind is my mom's favorite film, so I watched that quite early. Things that tap into that dreaminess and that weirdness and spookiness — that's up my alley. But it would be a dream to do a Before Sunrise kind of thing, where it's just two people talking for an hour and a half. I would love to do something like that next.

Is that what you're looking to do going forward then?

It could be anything. I really want to leave myself open. I would love to do something a little more scaled down, kind of dialogue-heavy thing. I could never have imagined the caliber of director and the caliber of actor that I've been working with. If I can only just continue to do that, I will be very lucky indeed. I've gotten to work with some of my absolute heroes, and that's been wonderful. But I want to keep working in horror as well. Horror's having a really exciting moment right now, especially young people in horror, with Obsession and Backrooms . I will stay as long as it'll have me. Horror, fantasy — that's what I grew up with, and I want to explore that more as well.

What does your ideal day off look like?

I would wake up at 10:30 a.m.-ish. I'm a very late-to-bed, late-to-rise kind of person in my free time. I'd wake up then; I'd get a coffee; I'd go for a walk. I have to do 10,000 steps a day. I'm like a dog. I have to be walked. Then I would go and see a movie. I would go to the cinema. I would probably go to the Prince Charles Cinema, which is my favorite in the world. I don't know whether I'd see it on my own or with somebody else. I do go on my own to the cinema a lot. That's one of my favorite ways to watch a film. Then I'd get a nice dinner. I might go shopping a little bit. I might go record shopping, go DVD shopping. Then I would go to the pub maybe, and then I would go to bed at 1 a.m. I'm being very specific with the times. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I'm unfamiliar with Prince Charles Cinema; why is that your favorite theater?

Just the vibe there, and the programming. There's always something on there that's worth seeing. I honestly have so much to thank that cinema for because the education in film that it has given me is just insane. I've seen so many films there for the first time. It's one of the few places, in London especially, where you can see old films and cult films and things that don't get screened very often. You can go and experience them in the theater, and that's a very valuable thing. They were going to possibly get shut down, but they've just won the battle against the landlord or whatever. They're going to be there for another 25 years. I'm very happy about that.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google New footage from Avengers: Doomsday has arrived and confirms the name of Victor Von Doom's son. The tragic backstory of Robert Downey Jr.'s Marvel villain has been teased for some time, with many theorizing that the multiverse tampering from other characters somehow resulted in the death of his wife and child. Marvel's first teaser poster for the film seemed to hint at this, showing a tapestry with a young boy and his mother that Doom stood under. Now, we know it's true.

A new TV spot for Avengers: Doomsday has made its way online, revealing plenty of new footage from the upcoming Marvel crossover . Though one bit of footage shows Johnny Storm in action as the Human Torch, it's the last bit of the TV spot that's the most distinct. By the end of the TV spot, not only do we get to see Steve Rogers wielding Mjolnir with a degree of power that definitely surpasses what we saw in Endgame , but we see him standing near a memorial in Latveria. On the memorial is the name of both Doom's wife and son, the latter being "Malachi Von Doom." Check it out for yourself below, but you may need a magnifying glass.

New ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’ teaser with new footage. In theaters December 18. pic.twitter.com/oTtGJ30YIB

The revelation that Doom's child is named Malachi Von Doom, and that he's deceased, confirms the fan theory about the Marvel villain's motivations. It also goes to show why he will have a bone to pick specifically with both Steve Rogers and Thor in the movie, since both characters will arrive in Doomsday with children. Steve's son was revealed in the most recent trailer, while Thor adopted Love at the end of his last solo movie. The name Malachi Von Doom also marks a change from the comics. Though Doom has previously had children in the pages of Marvel comics, none have had that specific name.

Steve showing off his powers while wielding Mjolnir in the new footage also shows that Chris Evans' hero has gotten something of an upgrade. Though he's been retired and living on another Earth, he never showed this level of power with Thor's hammer when he held it in Avengers: Endgame . That's good news for the former Avenger, because it's clear that Doom is a force to be reckoned with.

Ever since Avengers: Doomsday 's final trailer was released by Marvel this past week, the pre-verbal floodgates have seemingly been opened about new footage and plot points that were once closely guarded secrets. Marvel fans were quick to point this out this week when footage arrived of Ian McKellen's Magneto being glimpsed trying to remove Doom's mask, only to be overpowered by his magic. Today's footage continues the trend, though, and with three weeks left fans may end up dodging spoilers like Neo.

Are you worried about all the new Marvel spoilers arriving in the new Avengers: Doomsday footage? Or are you just ready to get in the theater and experience the whole thing? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Anime crossovers are surprisingly rare outside of merchandise campaigns, which will occasionally feature exclusive figures, plush toys, acrylic stands or illustrations. Sanrio is one such brand that regularly collabs with different anime series to release exclusive products, teaming up with properties like Jujutsu Kaisen and even Junji Ito's Tomie . However, it seems as though that trend may be moving in a new direction with some truly unexpected the announcement that an up-and-coming villainess series, Though I Am an Inept Villainess , will be sharing a special collaboration with Mothra in celebration of "Mothra Year."

Launched by Toho to celebrate Mothra's legacy in the Godzilla franchise and beyond, 2026 marks 65 years that the kaiju character has been on screen. The collaboration was a hit with the original author of Though I Am an Inept Villainess as well , expressing their delight on X (formerly Twitter) reacting to the promotional art. As it turns out, the artwork was requested by fans of the series due to a popular nickname attributed to Kou Reirin, or as she's referred to by fans, "His Highness's Mothra."

The origins of the Mothra Year and Inept Villainess collaboration art happens to be the result of enthusiastic fan effort. In the anime and novels, the main protagonist , Kou Reiren, is given the affectionate title of "His Highness's Butterfly." Due to events in the story, fans of the series have joked that Reiren is far too ferocious to be a simple butterfly giving her the much more apt title of "His Highness's Mothra."

In the art piece itself, this point is made obvious with Reiren being paired with Mothra, and her antagonistic narrative foil Keigetsu being paired next to Mothra's own in-universe counterpart Battra. TOHO produces both Inept Villainess as well as the Mothra film franchise, which gave fans the perfect opportunity to flood the studio with requests during TOHO's Mothra Year celebration.

Mothra Year is celebrating two major milestones in the Mothra franchise: the 65th anniversary of Mothra from 1961, as well the the 30th anniversary of the Rebirth of Mothra trilogy that released between 1996-1998. The year-long event has hosted a number of special celebrations for the kaiju icon, including special art exhibitions and pop-ups throughout Japan, as well as 4k Remasters of the original Mothra film and Godzilla vs. Mothra . TOHO also released the Rebirth of Mothra trilogy on Netflix .

Based on the original novels by Satsuki Nakamura, Though I Am an Inept Villainess 's anime adaptation is produced by Doga Kobo, a subsidiary of Kadokawa and TOHO that began airing during the Summer 2026 Anime Season . The series is available through anime streaming giants Crunchyroll and Hulu for anime fans in the United States. For those in Latin America, Canada and Europe, the series can be found on Disney+, and for fans in specific countries throughout Asia, Though I Am an Inept Villainess is available through Netflix. The first cour of the anime concluded in September 2026, with the anime slated to return in January 2027 to conclude its first season.

For those interested in reading the original work from Satsuki Nakamura, the light novel series of the same name is available in English through Seven Seas Entertainment, who, as of writing, have released twelve of the 13-volume series in both print and digital. Similarly, a manga adaptation with illustrations by Ei Ohitsuji is also available in English through Seven Seas Entertainment and has ten of its 11-volume series available for readers in the West.

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham 's office has spoken out against an upcoming Channel 4 documentary featuring an interview with disgraced former BBC presenter Huw Edwards .

Announced on Thursday, the doc sees Edwards — who, in 2024, was convicted of three counts of making indecent images of children — speak publicly about his downfall and criminal actions for the first time. Titled "Huw Edwards — Guilty," it's set to air on Channel 4 Dec. 1. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Beyoncé Makes Grammys History as First Artist With 100 Nominations Grammy Nominations 2027: Raye Leads With 11 Noms as Rosalía, Olivia Rodrigo, Ella Langley and Other Female Artists Dominate

The doc stirred up quite a bit of backlash in the U.K., and now Burnham has added his voice to the mix. In a statement to BBC News , an official spokesperson said: "Our thoughts first and foremost will be with the victims of child sexual abuse and exploitation. We have no interest in hearing what he has to say."

The spokesperson added, "There are extremely serious crimes and anyone convicted of them must face the consequences of their actions" and said the broadcasters "are expected to act responsibly and have appropriate regards to their audiences when making decisions."

articles.title: This Doomsday Essential MCU Watch List Will Have Marvel Fans Ready for Avengers 5 If You Start Today
articles.summary: We're less than one month from the release of Avengers: Doomsday, and Marvel die-hards are counting down the days. With just a few weeks before the film's release, and nearly twenty years of Marvel Studios' new releases making up the entire franchise, it might seem like Doomsday has a daunting amount of prep required to […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google We're less than one month from the release of Avengers: Doomsday , and Marvel die-hards are counting down the days. With just a few weeks before the film's release, and nearly twenty years of Marvel Studios' new releases making up the entire franchise, it might seem like Doomsday has a daunting amount of prep required to watch . The good news is that the upcoming movie is almost certainly designed to be new-viewer accessible, but for fans that want to make sure they're ready , the Doomsday Essential Watchlist is primed and easy to follow.

Marvel fans eager to get ready for the next epic crossover in the MCU, or anyone who just wants to catch up so they have no FOMO at Christmas time, Disney and Marvel previously released the Doomsday Essential Watchlist back at San Diego Comic-Con. Though it may seem like there's not enough time to cram everything in (there's no reason to watch all 38 MCU movies or all 18 TV shows), the good news is that if you start TODAY (November 27) and watch just one movie a day* from the Doomsday Essential Watchlist, you'll be in good shape for the actual theatrical release of Avengers: Doomsday . Here's the full calendar for you:

For the first two days, you're actually starting outside of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but with a franchise that has been around for more than two decades and holds a major place in the foundation of Avengers: Doomsday , the X-Men movies from 20th Century Fox.

Friday, November 27 - Watch X-Men (2000) Why It's Important : This film not only marked the feature film debut of the X-Men on the big screen, meaning it's the first appearance of key X-Men stars like James Marsden as Cyclops, Ian McKellen as Magneto, Hugh Jackman as Wolverine, Rebecca Romijn as Mystique, and, of course, Patrick Stewart as Professor X. Saturday, November 28 - Watch X2 (2003) Why It's Important : The sequel movie not only brought in more mutants that made a big impression, like Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler, but further established the world of the X-Men on the big screen and how the threats they face often force them to align their interests.

Sunday, November 29 - Watch Captain America: The First Avenger Why It's Important : Steve Rogers' origin story is not only one of the best Marvel movies, period, but delivers a story that will echo across the first three phases of the MCU with seeds that are paid off years later. Monday, November 30 - Watch Marvel's The Avengers Why It's Important : The first assembling of Earth's mightiest heroes remains one of the MCU's best accomplishments, and plants the seeds for conflicts that will continue to unfold across the next issues. It's also a turning point in Roger's story.

Tuesday, December 1 - Watch Avengers: Infinity War Why It's Important : The film not only brings Thanos into the picture as the big bad of the MCU, but shows off the many corners across the universe and how vast the entire team really is in the big picture. Plus, it shows the Avengers grappling with defeat. Wednesday, December 2 - Watch Avengers: Endgame Why It's Important: As Rocky says, it ain't about how hard you can hit, it's about how hard you can get hit and learn to get back up again. That's Avengers: Endgame in a nutshell, closing the narrative loops on its two bigest heroes, but also delivering a storyline that sets up Doomsday and Doom's fixations on messing with time.

Thursday, December 3 - Watch the first two episodes of Loki Why It's Important: The first episodes of the Disney+ series not only pick up a big storyline that is left completely hanging in Avengers: Endgame , with Loki escaping from the 2012 timeline with the Tesseract, but also introduce the concept of the multiverse and the TVA.

Friday, December 4 - Watch Loki Episodes 3 and 4 Why It's Important: The next batch of episodes of Loki are important because of how they continue to explore the idea of multiversal variants in the MCU, but also introduce The Void, essentially a garbage dump of pruned timelines.

Saturday, December 5 - Watch Loki Episodes 5 & 6 Why It's Important: The last two episodes bring two key antagonists into the MCU that play a big part in the road to Doomsday : Alioth, the creature that eats anything it can in The Void, and "He Who Remains," the Kang variant that created the TVA and teases a major multiversal threat.

Sunday, December 6 - Watch Loki Season 2, Episodes 1 & 2 Why It's Important: The second season of the series takes a darker shift, but also digs deeper into what can happen when someone starts messing with time and the multiverse in dangerous ways.

Monday, December 7 - Watch Loki Season 2, Episodes 3 & 4 Why It's Important: The mid-point of Season 2 takes the dangers of the multiverse to new levels, seemingly killing off major characters and leaving things in a place that a character like Doom in his own universe will almost certainly notice.

Tuesday, December 6 - Watch Loki Season 2, Episodes 5 & 6 Why It's Important: The last two episodes not only set up Loki's new place in the Marvel Cinematic Multiverse, but go on to tease the continued threat of Alioth in The Void as an endpoint for dead timelines.

Wednesday, December 9 - Watch Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings Why It's Important: One of the most important new characters in the MCU post-Endgame gets his debut here, but the 2021 Shang-Chi movie also teases the origin story of these titular ten rings, which appears to have a multiverse connection.

Thursday, December 10 - Watch Spider-Man: No Way Home Why It's Important: Though Loki will have well-prepared you for the idea of the multiverse and variants, it still didn't deliver quite on the scale that the 2021 Spider-Man film managed, bringing together decades and three different continuities of Spider-Man films to tell a story that will no doubt be important down the road.

Friday, December 11 - Watch Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness Why It's Important: Picking up after he cast that spell in No Way Home, not only does this film offer a look at how a character like Doctor Strange fits into things, but it brings us the first noted use of "incursions" in the MCU, puts Wanda Maximoff front and center, and brings Patrick Stewart back into the fold.

Saturday, December 12 - Watch Black Panther: Wakanda Forever Why It's Important: Though it's without question that the 2018 Black Panther movie is the superior film, the sequel is important for how it digs into the status of Wakanda and its titular superhero in the MCU moving forward, and that's on top of introducing Namor and Atlantis into the equation.

Sunday, December 13 - Watch Captain America: Brave New World Why It's Important: It might be easy to think that this film is skippable, but the way it establishes Sam Wilson as the new Cap and sets up him forming a new Avengers team is undeniably a big deal. There's also the fact that its main villain hints at something even bigger around the corner, perhaps indicating that he's been able to predict the incursions and even Doctor Doom himself.

Monday, December 14 - Watch Deadpool & Wolverine Why It's Important: Not only does this movie dig even deeper into the idea of variants, The Void, and the TVA, but it puts two heroes that were quietly confirmed to be in Avengers: Doomsday front and center.

Tuesday, December 15 - Watch Thunderbolts* Why It's Important: This is a big one not only because it has post-credit scenes that immediately setup Avengers: Doomsday , but it also confirms that Florence Pugh's Yelena is established as the new Black Widow of the MCU and puts an entire team together that will be integral to the film.

Wednesday, December 16 - Watch The Fantastic Four: First Steps Why It's Important: You couldn't have Victor Von Doom make his MCU debut without Marvel's first family, and the good news is that their MCU film is the best version yet of these classic comics on the big screen. It also doesn't hurt that the film ends with our first official look at Doom.

If you follow this watch order, not only will you be caught up with all the necessary MCU movies and TV shows to leap right into the narrative of Avengers: Doomsday , but you'll officially be caught up on the calendar. So, with that being said, the co-host stated that her motto this season was “apathy is the enemy.” She also had this to say about how people react to her fashion choices:

To that point, there were lots of moments on DWTS this year that got people on the internet talking, like liftgate , Jennifer Lawrence trolling Connor Wood , and Ezra Frech making it through his freestyle after his prosthetic fell off . Overall, Season 35 was met with a whole lot of love, but also quite a bit of intense discourse too. And yes, part of that had to do with Julianne Hough's fashion choices.

articles.title: Pokemon Just Revealed Two New Mega Evolutions, One of Which Is For a Beloved Legendary
articles.summary: The Pokemon Company has revealed the start date for Pokemon Champion's Regulation M-D, which will add two new Mega Evolutions to the game. While Mega Tatsugiri has long been awaited, primarily because fans hoped it would get Drizzle, Mega Heatran is the one making headlines and seeing players doomposting about how powerful it would be. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Pokemon Company has revealed the start date for Pokemon Champion's Regulation M-D, which will add two new Mega Evolutions to the game. While Mega Tatsugiri has long been awaited, primarily because fans hoped it would get Drizzle, Mega Heatran is the one making headlines and seeing players doomposting about how powerful it would be. Legendary Pokemon receiving Mega Evolutions is easily one of the biggest examples of power creep, and it is likely this addition will change the meta in Pokemon Champions going forward. It also suggests that future legendary Pokemon and their Mega Evolutions will likely be added to the game soon.

The Pokemon Company has confirmed that Mega Heatran and Mega Tatsugiri will be joining Pokemon Champions as part of Regulation Set M-D. The upcoming regulation will run from December 2, 2026, through March 3, 2027, introducing 24 additional Pokemon and four Mega Evolutions. Heatran, Tatsugiri, and Dondozo are the only confirmed additions, but fans are already speculating on what the other two Mega Evolutions will be in Mega Latios and Mega Latias. These powerful Megas will be a major threat, as will the combination of Dondozo and Tatsugiri.

Heatran was introduced in Pokemon Diamond and Pearl and has stood among other legendary Pokemon because of its Steel and Fire-type combination. Not only that, but it has consistently been a meta threat, especially when paired with the Assault Vest. Mega Heatran will make it even more terrifying, and its Water Compaction ability will make it a physical powerhouse. Fans are already pairing it alongside Aqua Jet Primarina and planning to use it in Trick Room.

Regulation M-D begins on December 2! In Regulation M-D, you'll be able to use Mega Heatran, Dondozo, and Mega Tatsugiri in battle! #PokemonChampions pic.twitter.com/J5VyNOdCPm

Mega Tatsugiri is the more interesting addition, as fans have been waiting for this Pokemon ever since Pokemon Champions was released . The hope was it would gain Drizzle and be the Mega weather setter for rain teams, but its ability actually increases its Special Attack when it hits the field, making it much more threatening than its base form. But the more impactful addition of Tatsugiri is its partner, Dondozo, which is considered one of the biggest menaces in Pokemon.

It remains to be seen how either Mega Evolution will affect the meta , as both offer different playstyles. Regulation Set M-D will also arrive alongside a balance update that sees changes to abilities like Flash Fire and Pokemon gaining access to new moves. With existing Pokemon remaining eligible for Ranked Battles, the upcoming additions should give competitive players plenty of opportunities to revisit their favorite teams. It won't be long until players have to deal with these changes, as well as the possibility that Mega Latios and Mega Latias will also be added to Pokemon Champions .
