articles.title: 5 Best Black Friday Steam Sales to Take Advantage Of
articles.summary: Courtesy of Valve Black Friday is here for 2026, creating a number of deals on Steam for players to check out for the next couple of weeks. Although the length of certain deals may vary, there are several bundles and individual discounts players should check out right away, especially for some of the biggest releases of the last […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Black Friday is here for 2026, creating a number of deals on Steam for players to check out for the next couple of weeks. Although the length of certain deals may vary, there are several bundles and individual discounts players should check out right away, especially for some of the biggest releases of the last year. With some games providing dozens to hundreds of hours worth of experiences, their Black Friday prices are even more impressive as the holiday season of deals truly begins for the year.

Although this List will mainly be exploring deals for singular games, there are some great Black Friday bundles worth investigating too. Fighting game fans should check out Steam's discount for a collection including Under Night In-Birth 2 Sys: Celes , Guilty Gear Strive , and BlazBlue Central Fiction , which totals to $19.50 on a 85% marked down price. Ordinarily, the base versions of these games together would cost $129.97, making this one of many great Black Friday deals you should check out over the upcoming Thanksgiving 2026 weekend.

One of the top selling games on Steam is Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth , which makes sense, considering that Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is set to release in February 2027 next year. Before the finale of the FF7 remake trilogy comes to end, players can explore the middle chapter through an 85% discount, making a $49.99 game only $7.49. Monetarily, this is clearly one of the best deals for Steam on Black Friday, especially since Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth is a much larger game than FF7 Remake Intergrade before it.

FF7 Rebirth follows the same path as the original Final Fantasy 7 , taking players out of Midgar and into the much larger world, giving them much larger open areas to explore with their party. New characters like Red XIII and Cait Sit provide new play styles for combat alongside familiar favorites like Cloud, Barret, Tifa, and Aerith from the previous remake. All parts of the game have been expanded too, from gear and inventory systems to the combat itself, which now includes special team-up attacks between characters. At the same time, new extensive mini-games like Queen's Blood and Fort Condor make playing FF7 Rebirth even more worth the small price point it's currently listed at.

ARC Raiders is an extraction shooter that's perfect for you and your friends to play during the holidays, offering both PvE and PvP content to appeal to any group's preferences. As one of the multiplayer games nominated for a Game Award in 2026, ARC Raiders has received praise for its immersive world, which has evolving maps that makes multiplayer adventures feel organic and dynamic as conditions on the map change. Rather than the condensed, linear nature of battle royale games and other live service titles, ARC Raiders has a greater sense of unpredictability, giving it a replay value other extraction shooters fail to reach.

For Black Friday, Steam is offering ARC Raiders for 50% lower of its normal price, taking it down from $39.99 to $19.99. This is for the Standard Edition of the game, of course, putting you in a blank state to get your adventure started. Although the game is not without problems, facing criticism for overblown player hacking and slight AI usage, getting togther with a group of friends easily makes those issues minimal. Finding ways to complete quests and and grow stronger through collected gear is satisfying, providing dozens of hours of steady progression through engaging gunplay.

While released originally in 2020, Crusader Kings 3 is getting a new major expansion titled "Silk and Silver" in November 2026, likely also creating its astounding Black Friday deal this year. On Steam, this game is only $14.99 rather than $49.99, indicating a remarkable 70% off deal for one of the decade's more fascinating strategy games. While Star Wars: Zero Company and Hearts of Iron 4 are also brilliant strategy titles on sale for Black Friday, Crusader Kings 3 might be the most detailed, having players rule over a sprawling empire that they need to manage at all times. Maintaining a noble bloodline isn't easy though, as guiding a dynasty takes some real work.

Huge maps in this game combine with extensive mechanics tied to securing land, bestowing titles, and maintaining a vast array of vassals to keep your rule. Creating complex schemes is part of the strategy in Crusader Kings 3 , with using Game of Thrones level tactics to keep your family in line with your wishes. You could rule through an iron fist, blackmail your way through politics, or be a generous ruler who is beloved through magnanimous deeds. Rivals are ever-present and culture is always evolving, making runs of Crusader Kings 3 long affairs that will keep you engaged for a good period of time.

The beauty of 007 First Light being on sale for Black Friday this year is how it is being marked down at the perfect time, with recent news of the latest James Bond actor making this game shine even more. While the latest movie featuring the iconic spy is in the works, players can jump into IO Interactive's take on James Bond, in the same formula as the studio's celebrated Hitman games. 007 First Light is easily the best Bond game since GoldenEye , featuring a great rendition of the character and plenty of features that pay homage to what makes the figure special across media.

For starters, James Bond is played to great effect by actor Patrick Gibson, who brings the perfect balance of charm and wit to a younger version of Bond in his first days within MI6. The immature snark of Bond is genuinely endearing in the game, which lends itself to a compelling story with the visual and musical beats of the best 007 movies out there. As far as gameplay is concerned, 007 First Light adopts many mechanics from Hitman , putting players in large sandboxes to accomplish missions however they see fit. This non-linear approach greatly encourages player choice and freedom, with stealth and creativity at the forefront of their efforts.

Players can infiltrate parts of a map with a quick one-liner, or use their License to Kill to eliminate enemy forces toward a target of interest. Unlike Hitman , mission goals are usually more open-ended, creating a varying game flow that is constantly interesting to figure out. For those excited for the next James Bond movie, 007 First Light is a great one to try out for just $34.99 during Black Friday sales, rather than the $69.99 original price. This game is up for several Game Awards for this year as well, once again reinforcing its quality among other 2026 titles.

Kingdom Come Deliverance 2 is one of the best RPGs of the last few years, having a level of immersive quality that hasn't been challenged since the recent launch of GTA 6 . Much like Rockstar's monumental hit, Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is a game you can sink hundreds of hours into due to the sheer number of details present at every step. In the beginning, you are just a peasant with no skill in anything, but gradually, you can do various tasks to increase your stats one at a time to become a skilled presence in a historically accurate medieval world.

Everything in this game requires attention, from meticulous combat to learning recipes to craft various items with different benefits. Although a simple story about a journey to avenge your parents, the destiny of protagonist Henry is mainly up to you, with deep story telling choices shaping your adventure. It's absolutely addicting to get into the side quests and skill progressive content of this game, with players sometimes spending 30+ hours or more into the title without starting the first quest. Reputation as you travel matters too, with quests progressing with or without you and your impact in certain regions being felt dozens of hours after you acted in those areas.

Steam is listing Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 for a shocking $19.79 rather than $59.99, a steal considering the game's longevity and value. Few games manage to make a world that feels like it is truly living and breathing alongside you, through actually interesting NPCs to the freedom to make your own choices. Much like Baldur's Gate 3 or GTA 6 , Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is a great Black Friday game for players who want to see their choices leave an impact in the game they're playing.

articles.content:
Tyson Fury does not have schizophrenia and a scene in which his wife claims he does has been edited out of the Netflix movie about the British boxing superstar.

The doc, titled Tyson Fury, provides a tell-all account of Fury's mental health struggles as he builds up to his fight with Anthony Joshua next month, which is also on Netflix.

The trailer initially showed Fury's wife Paris Fury saying the boxer is a "mild schizophrenic," but amid questions from the boxing regulator, this has now been revealed to be untrue. articles.title: Tucker Carlson Sounded Like Jeremy Culhane’s SNL Impression While Explaining Why He Won’t Watch It
articles.summary: You need to read this article. That's the rule.
articles.content:
If you’re wondering what Tucker Carlson thinks of breakout SNL star Jeremy Culhane ’s buzzy impression, the unfortunate truth is we may never know. The popular talking head has apparently never seen it, and it’s not because he’s angry about it or opposed on principle, it’s because he’s against consuming any articles or videos about himself.

If that quote did something to you, it’s probably because Tucker uses one of the Tucker-isms Culhane uses all the time in his impression. It feels like every SNL appearance includes at least a couple usages of, “That’s the rule.” It warmed my heart to see it here, and it made me even more impressed with Culhane’s impression, given it almost felt in character the way Carlson said it. Seriously, first check out the interview with Carlson in real life…

I love how Straka basically has a panic attack the second he says, “That’s my rule.” In that moment, he’s all of us freaking out because he just said the thing. If you listen closely to the rest of Tucker’s comments, however, you can hear a lot more of where Culhane’s impression comes from. There’s the cadence in how he speaks, and of course there’s the signature laugh that Carlson has been known for throughout his career.

After his initial comments about never having seen the impression, Carlson went on to talk more generally about being parodied, and he had some really thoughtful things to say about his place in the world and what it’s like to get older. He said when he was a kid, he would look at older people and wonder if they were doing a bit, but as he’s aged and gotten feedback from his kids, he’s slowly realized that everyone sort of becomes a caricature of themselves.

It sounds like Carlson is never going to watch Culhane’s impression, but I would love to see a reaction video of him checking it out for the first time, especially since he has more free reign outside Fox News . I wonder what would be going through his head, especially since it feels like a slightly exaggerated but also pretty realistic take on him as a talking head. It's hard to tell because celebrities have a wide range of opinions about getting parodied on the show. Elon Musk, as an example, doesn't like Culhane's take on him .

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google We had some peak animated series in the '90s, evolving from the cookie-cutter shows of the prior decade that were still great but arguably on a different level. The animation was more fluid and lively, the characters were bigger and bolder, and the genres were pushed to their limits as far as what was expected from a kids show. As the darker superhero shows like Batman: The Animated Series and X-Men began to gain steam and reshape Saturday mornings, another geeky genre began to rise up back into prominence, leaving some very influential albeit oft-forgotten cartoons in its wake.

Sci-Fi shows have historically had a tricky time finding their footing when it comes to children's television, and even moreso for cartoons. Many of them barely lasted thirteen episodes, and those that made it beyond that point were lucky to squeeze out a few seasons before being abruptly cancelled with no chance to conclude their arcs. That didn't make these shows any less special or meaningful, earning a place in our hearts and minds for years to come and opening the gateway for more sci-fi as we grew up. Here are five animated series for kids from the 90's that offered something completely different from the typical Saturday morning toons, and that hold up as perfect examples of sci-fi at its best that deserve a second look.

Exosquad was an Americanized version of Japanese adult anime aimed at children. If that sounds confusing, that just means you never watched the show before. Influenced by shows like Mobile Suit Gundam and Macross that were as big on mechs as they were complex storytelling, Exosquad was humanity's last stand against Neosapiens, a race of genetically engineered beings made by Earth's residents to become their workers and instead became its oppressors through a huge role reversal and uprising. Suited up in their E-Frames, JT Marsh's Able Squad took the fight to the stars in large-scale battles that would impress the most discerning Star Wars fans. Unlike most of its contemporaries, Exosquad had one ongoing story where every episode mattered to the overall story arc of liberating Earth from the Neosapiens.

War is never fun, and Exosquad made sure its viewers understood the weight of what was happening amid its brightly colored mech battles and starships. It was fairly mature and as dark as it could be for its time, and would easily be one of the first candidates I would pick on this list for a modern gritty reboot since it would hardly need any changes to make it more adult. The show wrapped after two seasons, leaving its fans behind with a cliffhanger ending that would have introduced a new villain that would force the humans and Neosapiens to put aside their differences and work together to keep the peace in the galaxy. The biggest theme across this list will be these shows all ended too soon before they could truly end their series, and Exosquad will forever be one of my favorite shows that needed more time to finish its story.

I recently wrote about the life and times of this oddball anthropomorphic franchise , and briefly touched on its short-lived animated series, describing it as a cross between Star Wars and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles . It was futuristic furry animals fighting space battles with laser pistols against a megalomaniacal military-industrial complex run by toads with plans for universal domination, so in some ways this was actually closer to Star Wars multiplied. Human Willy DeWitt helps kids watching at home have a character they can identify with, but he was barely a footnote in this crazy list of psychic cats, mercenary foxes, and sharpshooting waterfowl.

The crew of the Righteous Indignation crossed paths with bounty hunting purple alligators, frog-shaped mechs and Beetlegeusian Baboons, fighting the good fight like any interplanetary rebel alliance would against an evil empire of corporate stooges with the power to build an army. With a paltry 12 episodes under one season, Bu cky O'Hare and the Toad Wars is an easy watch if you can find it. It's a true shame this series never had more of a chance to complete its story across both animation and comic books, as there were clearly some places they wanted to go as far as storylines that never saw fruition. Don't be fooled by the cute animals and silly sounding concept. Bucky O'Hare is the real deal and he deserves some respect on his name. Plus, he has the best theme song of any cartoon on this list!

Superior to the majority of the cinematic sequels, Highlander: The Animated Series continued the tales of the MacLeod family and their quest for the Prize — but that's where the similarities between the movies and this cartoon end. Set centuries ahead of the rest of the franchise in a dystopian 27th century landscape, Quentin MacLeod learns that he is an immortal as well the last of his ancestry. With the tutelage of Ramirez (a different one from the Sean Connery version in the original movie) and help from his sister Clyde and Snarf-coded pet Gaul, the group travel the ruined world to battle and learn from the other immortals as they prepare for a showdown with the planet's dictator, Kortan.

A combination of fantasy and sci-fi wrapped into one, Highlander: The Animated Series was surprisingly violent for a show made for young kids. Even though they introduced a way to gain an immortal's powers without decapitating their foes, heads still rolled along with the on-screen deaths of many characters across the show's two seasons. Imagine if Fist of the North Star received a treatment by Disney, and you'd have a sense for how Highlander's swordfights played out — but even then you might still be surprised by how far they pushed Standards & Practices. The worldbuilding is top notch along with some good characters and storytelling that found a way to make an R-rated movie not only accessible to kids, but made something superb that honors the source material while creating something brand new.

Have you ever wondered what happens when you put a video game inside a console? Reboot answered that question with snazzy 1994 CGI graphics and self-contained episodes that used many classic video game genres, movies and TV shows to show off a unique virtual world unlike any that kids had seen on a Saturday morning before. It was like if Tron met Toy Story , but with a dose of The Matrix long before that existed. Every episode was a thrilling adventure, but there was also a larger story being played out that quietly shifted the tone from shenanigans into something more serious.

Reboot lasted for four seasons, with a three-year gap of production time between the third and final fourth season. Its last season revealed many secrets about the lore of the Mainframe, and ended on an unresolved cliffhanger that the shows creator still refuses to tell anyone. By then, things had become much darker and different from its first days on air, but this was a welcome change. The show remains a cult favorite, with many of its episodes viewable on Mainframe Studio's official YouTube channel. Reboot remains a very fun and often forgotten piece of 90's Saturday morning sci-fi

Nearly a decade after the original Transformers wrapped up their four season run, Beast Wars roared into action in September, 1996. The first series in the franchise to be fully animated using CGI (by the same folks behind Reboot ), Beast Wars removed the modern vehicles and placed the heroic Maximals and foul Predacons on prehistoric Earth, giving them organic forms instead of mechanical ones. The teams of warring factions were also significantly smaller than their predecessors, leaving more space for deeper character development and complex relationships that weren't so easy to do with a series that had dozens of characters vying for attention.

While Beast Wars had its share of light-hearted episodes (you could always rely on Waspinator for a laugh) or others focused purely on action, some delved into more serious waters like "Transmutate" and "Crossing the Rubicon." It also managed to connect the original 80's cartoon, proving that not even time and space can keep Starscream from being a nuisance to the good guys. After three excellent seasons, the show transitioned into "Beast Machines," which brought the heroes back to their home planet of Cybertron, but its one in which they lost and Megatron rules the world. This darker sequel series hit on many high sci-fi concepts, and is a must-watch companion if you plan on binging Beast Wars . Combined, they're a pair of unusual entries in the Transformers series, but that is what makes them such perfect parts of the franchise that should never be overlooked against its more mechanical-looking counterparts.

Did we miss your favorite 90's Saturday morning cartoon that was an example of awesome sci-fi? Join the conversation and let us know about it in the comments.

articles.title: People Keep Sleeping On Two Fantastic Apple TV Shows, And I’ve Had Enough
articles.summary: The horses aren’t slow, but monkeys are a little bad!
articles.content:
Apple TV, in my opinion, consistently puts out some of the highest-quality shows of any streamer, and it seems like too many people sleep on a couple of the best: Slow Horses and Bad Monkey . The latter of which just kicked off its second season on the 2026 TV schedule , and that makes now the perfect time to jump on a great Black Friday deal for an Apple subscription .

Unless you’ve been living under a rock lately, you have probably seen a ton about GTA: VI and how it's set in a fictional version of Florida, and it’s filled with wild characters and kooky situations that only Florida can provide. You don’t have to be a gamer to get a similar experience with Bad Monkey . The show stars Vince Vaughn as a washed-up detective who gets himself wrapped up in some truly oddball cases in Florida.

It’s also a book-to-screen adaptation based on a work by Carl Hiaasen, who is the king of bringing the weirdest bits of Florida to life, especially the kinds of totally goofy characters that make that state so unique, fun, and strange. Hiaasen was creating “Florida Mans” long before that became a thing. The show is just as fun as any of Hiaasen's books and really captures the spirit of everything he writes about.

The second show I feel like too many people sleep on is Slow Horses , based on the Slough House series by author Mick Herron. This isn’t a comedy like Bad Monkey , though Gary Oldman plays easily one of the funniest characters on TV these days. It’s a spy show about a group of disgraced MI5 agents in London led by a washed-up old Cold Warrior named Jackson Lamb (Oldman).

articles.title: With A New LOTR Movie Coming, Orlando Bloom Talks His Own Legacy
articles.summary: One ring to bind them.
articles.content:
I can still hardly believe a new Lord of the Rings movie is coming down the pipeline. Directed by Andy Serkis, the Aragorn road trip journey The Hunt for Gollum is already filming with the director also back in the mo-cap suit , and we got some first look set photos earlier this year. Now, as the movie continues to come together ahead of its 2027 movie release , franchise OG Orlando Bloom talks his own legacy in the franchise.

We’d actually spoken to Bloom when he was recast as Legolas in The Hobbit trilogy and asked him how he felt about getting to return to the world a second time. He told CinemaBlend it was “sheer joy, ” although there were some practical concerns about having aged a decade since the original LOTR films.

They did bridge that gap, and Bloom looked great in The Hobbit movies. I think it’s very interesting the new movie The Hunt for Gollum will also be bringing another elf back a decade later once more with Lee Pace reprising Thranduil (Legolas' father), so while elves live on and on, the humans behind the movies face some practical challenges. Still, Bloom believes it's a privilege to be a part of Tolkien's story (and recent his words echo newcomer Anya Taylor-Joy's feelings as well.)

There's no indication right now Orlando Bloom will be back on set for another round, though he does have his own LOTR reunion coming in a different project. Regardless, given the timeline of the movie, which plays out just before The Fellowship of the Ring , the elven world will once again be a part of The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt For Gollum . The legacy that Orlando Bloom helped created should live on in this new movie, and I, for one, can't wait to see what that looks like.

The Royal Ruby […]

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Want to get behind the wheel of a Progen Emerus without waiting until later in GTA 6 ? You're in luck. Two custom versions of this high-performance supercar can be stolen during the story, giving players an opportunity to grab one of Leonida's most exciting rides without having to track down a dealership.

The Royal Ruby Emerus is the more straightforward option, sitting inside a guarded property on Vespucci Island. There's also a purple variant waiting at a robbery location on Waxman Island, although you'll need to make enough progress for that opportunity to appear. Here's where to find both cars and how to drive away with them.

The Royal Ruby Emerus is located at a mansion on Vespucci Island , one of the Rialto Islands east of Vice City. Head to the western side of the island and look for Neptune Circle , just south of the main road. You'll find a large property with a locked gate, and the red supercar is waiting inside. Getting onto the grounds is the first challenge, as the property is guarded and you won't be able to simply stroll through the entrance unnoticed.

Climb over the gate or find another way into the grounds, then make your way toward the garage on the southern side of the house . The Royal Ruby Emerus should be parked inside, ready for the taking. Once you've reached the car, climb into the driver's seat and make your escape. You'll need to get back through the property gate, so be prepared to deal with any guards who spot you before you can get onto the road. Unlike some of the more heavily secured vehicles in GTA 6 , this Emerus doesn't require a Key Cloner to steal.

If you're after something a little more colorful, there's another custom Emerus at Chatfield Storage & Logistics on Waxman Island. The island sits east of downtown Vice City, between the Rialto Islands and Catalan Bay . Look toward its western side for the storage facility, where a purple Emerus can be found during a Robbery Opportunity . Keep an eye out for the yellow Robbery Opportunity marker on your map. If it hasn't appeared yet, continue progressing through the story until the opportunity becomes available.

When you approach Chatfield Storage & Logistics, you'll see the purple Emerus enter the yard before the gate closes behind it. You'll have to get into the facility and deal with the armed guards protecting the property before making your move. Once the area is clear, search the shipping containers and the surrounding yard for the car. Its exact position can vary depending on how the encounter unfolds , so don't assume it's always parked in the same spot. Fortunately, the Emerus itself isn't protected by a lock or security system, meaning you can get behind the wheel once you've reached it.

articles.title: The Witcher 4 Boss Puts Xbox Fans at Ease After New PlayStation Partnership
articles.summary: When CD Projekt RED and Sony announced a partnership for The Witcher 4, fans were understandably concerned about console exclusivity. Thankfully, the developer has wasted little time addressing those concerns, confirming that PlayStation's involvement does not mean Ciri's upcoming adventure will skip Xbox consoles. Console exclusivity has long been a frustrating aspect of the gaming […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When CD Projekt RED and Sony announced a partnership for The Witcher 4 , fans were understandably concerned about console exclusivity. Thankfully, the developer has wasted little time addressing those concerns, confirming that PlayStation's involvement does not mean Ciri's upcoming adventure will skip Xbox consoles. Console exclusivity has long been a frustrating aspect of the gaming industry, particularly when a beloved multiplatform franchise suddenly favors one platform over another. While Sony appears to be more involved with The Witcher 4 than previous entries, Xbox and PC players should still expect to play the game according to CD Projekt RED's CEO, Michal Nowakowski.

CD Projekt RED revealed that it has entered a marketing agreement with Sony for The Witcher 4 . This partnership should function similarly to how Rockstar Games and Sony heavily promoted Grand Theft Auto 6 for the PlayStation 5. Naturally, when the announcement was first made, fans assumed that the studio's next game would be exclusive to the PS5, but Nowakowski has assured fans that this is not the case and there are no plans to leave anyone behind for The Witcher 4 or other CD Projekt RED projects.

Following the announcement of the PlayStation partnership, Nowakowski took to social media to express his excitement while reaffirming CD Projekt Red's commitment to multiplatform releases.

"We’re looking forward to our partnership with PlayStation!” Nowakowski said. “And just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform."

We’re looking forward to our partnership with PlayStation! And just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform. https://t.co/9X7YEvxHI2

The agreement appears to be strictly focused on marketing, which will likely see The Witcher 4 featured heavily in PlayStation's marketing campaigns. This should be no surprise considering how beloved The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is, especially with the remaster and upcoming DLC. It should be noted that this does not necessarily mean the game will run better or get exclusive perks on PS5.

Hopefully this will see a better launch than Cyberpunk 2077 on PS5 . Sony actually pulled the game from the PlayStation Store following multiple bugs and issues. The RPG has since returned to the PS Store and is one of the highest-rated games on the platform. But all this shows how the relationship between CD Projekt RED and Sony has grown, resulting in this partnership for The Witcher 4 .

There is still no confirmed release date for The Witcher 4 , but fans may learn something soon at the 2026 Game Awards. Alternatively, with this partnership, Sony may actually be the ones to share a launch date, meaning fans should be paying attention to PlayStation's socials and online channels. But regardless of which platform features most prominently in its advertising, players can look forward to experiencing Ciri's adventure together.

articles.title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles’ Matthew Rosenberg Teases No Feelings Spared in War All the Time [EXCLUSIVE]
articles.summary: With November coming to an end, we’re getting ever closer to 2027 but it’s not just a new year on the horizon, at least not for the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. The beloved heroes are headed into a new era when Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #25 hits comic shops on January 13th. Following the epic […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google With November coming to an end, we’re getting ever closer to 2027 but it’s not just a new year on the horizon, at least not for the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. The beloved heroes are headed into a new era when Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #25 hits comic shops on January 13th. Following the epic runs from writer Jason Aaron and artist Juan Ferreyra and then writer Gene Luen Yang and artist Freddie E. Williams II , the Turtles are getting a new creative team in January with writer Matthew Rosenberg and artist Juann Cabal and it might just be the most action-packed yet.

After “The City That Never Dies” we embark on “War All the Time” and the biggest fight in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles history. It’s poised to be an exciting time for not just long-time fans but newcomers to the world of the Turtles as well. ComicBook had a chance to talk with Rosenberg about his upcoming Turtles run and not only does he tease going “bigger and bigger” with a story that is also rooted in family drama, but it sounds like there might be some things in the works for Shredder fans, too.

ComicBook: You’re the third writer for this series and the first two had 12 issues each, basically telling one big story. Do you see your run as telling one self-contained story, or laying the groundwork for something bigger down the line?

Matthew Rosenberg: Well, my first arc is only 6 issues and all takes place in one night. SO, if I say something stupid or everyone hates it that might be it. But assuming that doesn’t happen, we are already working on our next arc and it’s one of the biggest and most ambitious things I’ve ever written. It’s really fun to get the chance to just play with all the toys in the toy chest. I’m a really big fan of Dan Watters. Not as a person, he’s awful. But his work on Shredder has been amazing. So, we’ve been talking about ways to build off what he’s been doing. It’s going to be one the Turtles fans won’t want to miss.

It feels like the Turtles are in a transitionary period right now, and issue #25 promises an old enemy and more coming back. Do you see this as a return to basics for the team, or the start of something brand-new?

With legacy characters like this it’s always a mix. Even in the last two years with what Jason Aaron and Gene Luen Yang were writing in their books, they were miles apart from each other in some ways, but very much connected in others. For this first arc we are trying to do a back-to-basics approach, a sort of homage to the Eastman and Laird original run and just remind everyone why they cared about 4 slimy brothers who were ready to take on the whole world. Only in our run they just might have to.

In this series so far, the Turtles have faced threats both very grounded and massively fantastical. They’re known for juggling all that and some serious sci-fi, but which aspect does this upcoming issue and run lean into the most?

We’re opening on a street level brawl. That’s what the Turtles were born out of and that’s where we can show off who they are at their core and why they matter so much. And from there, we’re just going bigger and bigger.

Your upcoming “War All the Time” arc promises to evoke classics like Daredevil: Born Again, so how much of the threat is something the TMNT need to physically overcome, and how much is going to be major family drama?

It’s always going to be rooted in family drama. How each brother deals with things, what they value, what they’re willing to do, all serve to create the tension. But yeah, a whole lot of people are trying to kill them too. So sometimes the family drama will take the backseat to, ya know, not getting murdered. But it’s going to be a fight all the way across the city and nobody’s feelings are being spared.

Here’s how IDW describes Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #25: “It’s all-out war as New York’s own Matthew Rosenberg takes over the TMNT! After ’The City That Never Dies,’ it’s been quiet in New York City…a little too quiet. But a newly resurrected old enemy is determined to make some noise for our Heroes in a Half-Shell. One city. Countless villains. The biggest fight in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles history starts here, as our Turtles fight ‘War All the Time.’”

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #25 hits stores on January 13, 2027, from IDW Publishing. Pre-orders for the issue are due November 30th.

articles.title: GTA 6 Was Nearly a Whole Lot More Like Animal Crossing Before Rockstar Removed Certain Features
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has one of the most impressive and immersive open worlds, but Rockstar Games nearly made it more like Animal Crossing before cutting certain cozy features. While the series is primarily associated with elaborate heists, high-speed police chases, and criminal enterprises, there is plenty of downtime. Players almost had an additional handful […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Grand Theft Auto 6 has one of the most impressive and immersive open worlds, but Rockstar Games nearly made it more like Animal Crossing before cutting certain cozy features. While the series is primarily associated with elaborate heists, high-speed police chases, and criminal enterprises, there is plenty of downtime. Players almost had an additional handful of activities to enjoy, including being able to decorate their homes. Yet Rockstar ultimately cut this feature and many others that would have given players more to do with Lucia that didn't involve crime.

Some of the cut activities in GTA 6 were decorating your home, crafting, tennis, movie theaters, crawling, and more. Each was cut for its own reason, whether it was not interactive enough or time simply ran out, but would likely have been wonderful additions to the game. The home decoration and crafting instantly feel familiar to Animal Crossing: New Horizons and could have given GTA 6 a cozy vibe that the series has lacked in the past. Future updates could add this content back, or it may be saved for GTA 6 Online , but there is no guarantee we'll ever see it.

During an interview with PC Games , Rockstar North's Rob Nelson and Scott Mitchell discussed several gameplay features that didn't survive development. The studio spent considerable time exploring mechanics that would have allowed players to furnish their homes, craft items, and crawl along the ground. The pair specifically point to tennis, but Rockstar wasn't satisfied with its execution and scrapped it.

Home decorating is arguably the most disappointing omission here. One of the biggest appeals of Animal Crossing: New Horizons and other cozy games is how satisfying this is, and many players immediately fell in love with Jason's first house. Collecting furniture, experimenting with different layouts, and decorating as you see fit would have added so many layers to Jason and Lucia's home life, as well as making players more attached to their safehouses.

Crafting would have complemented this system, particularly if it was an expanded version of the system introduced in Red Dead Redemption 2 . Collecting resources throughout Leonida could have served a purpose beyond exploration, allowing players to create decorations, equipment, or other useful items. Both systems could have been optional but added more depth to the game and given cozy players a different experience.

It is understandable why Rockstar cut some features. Time crunch, even with the game's delays and long development time, makes it hard to include every feature. Likewise, some features just may not have had the payoff developers hoped for and were cut to keep the game enjoyable. That said, these would be wonderful updates Rockstar could bring to Grand Theft Auto 6 and give players more to do in free roam.

EXCLUSIVE : Toronto-based film and TV company Wildling Pictures has optioned Emily McBride’s psychological folk horror novel Queen Mab and Jason Bell’s WWII spy story Operation Sparrow , with a view to turning both into features.

Published in September this year, Bell’s archival research uncovers a little known but significant espionage operation from WWII which helped protect the D-Day landings. Drawing on newly declassified OSS files, the spy thriller "tells the true story of three American officers who parachuted into Nazi-allied Hungary in 1944 on a mission designed to end in their capture. Operation Sparrow is Wildling’s second option of Jason Bell’s work following the optioning of his book Cracking the Nazi Code , which Wildling is developing with screenwriter Adam Yorke ( Phreaker, See For Me) . The production company has also acquired the rights to Canadian author Emily McBride’s debut novel Queen Mab, the psychological folk horror which was released this summer. Screenwriter and director Emily O’Quinn Code ( Fresh Meat Mom, Bush Skeleton ) is onboard to write the screenplay.

The well-received novel "follows a young scholar of fairy lore, Madeleine, as she loses her grip on reality to postpartum psychosis and must outwit her own logic before it drives her to do what the folklore prescribes."

Both projects are grounded in European settings and stories. Queen Mab is rooted in British and Irish folklore, while Operation Sparrow is rooted in Hungary and wider Central Europe. Wildling is currently in early discussions with potential global co-production partners across the UK, Ireland and the rest of Europe to develop the films for the international market. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Wildling’s slate of literary adaptations also includes coming-of-age romantic comedy Laura Dean Keeps Breaking Up with Me , based on Mariko Tamaki’s graphic novel and co-produced with MXN Entertainment and Good Girl. The film stars Ava Phillippe and Sam Morelos and is directed by Tommy Dorfman.

Matt Code, producer and President of Wildling Pictures, said: “Both Queen Mab and Operation Sparrow have the potential to open up their worlds on screen. Emily McBride has created a psychologically rich story that draws on the depth of British and Irish folklore, while Jason brings a hidden chapter of WWII history to light. Identifying these rich and distinctive literary IPs is a central part of Wildling’s approach to developing projects with both creative ambition and international reach and they’re a key part of our literary slate expansion.”

Recent original productions for Wildling include Young Werther (TIFF 2024, Special Presentations) and Paying for It (TIFF 2024, Platform), as well as the comedy Suze (Santa Barbara International Film Festival 2024) and the thriller See for Me (Tribeca 2021, released in over 25 territories).

The company has just wrapped production on its latest feature Devour starring Tricia Helfer, and written and directed by Erica Orofino. Recent features include Adam Yorke’s debut feature Phreaker, which had its world premiere at Fantastic Fest. The company is also developing the feature documentary Skinnamarink Forever: The Sharon, Lois & Bram Story. Recent service credits include Motorheads (Jax Media/Amazon) Dream Scenario (A24) and Hell of a Summer (Neon), both of which premiered at TIFF 2023.

On the television side, Wildling is currently developing Elias , an original dark comedy and official selection of the 2026 TIFF Series Creator Lab from Emily O’Quinn Code, the novel Clara Voyant by Rachelle Delaney into a one-hour series, and Professor Goose , a preschool animated series based on the books by Paulette Bourgeois and Alex G. Griffiths.

articles.title: Iranian Activist and 'It Was Just an Accident' Screenwriter Mehdi Mahmoudian Arrested in Tehran on Charges of 'Anti-Government Propaganda'
articles.summary: Iranian activist Mehdi Mahmoudian, who is also the co-writer of revered auteur Jafar Panahi's Palme d'Or-winning drama "It Was Just an Accident," has been arrested at his home in Tehran, according to several sources. Mahmoudian, who is a human rights defender and political journalist, was taken away by police agents from his home on Wednesday […]
articles.content:
Iranian activist Mehdi Mahmoudian , who is also the co-writer of revered auteur Jafar Panahi 's Palme d'Or-winning drama "It Was Just An Accident," has been arrested at his home in Tehran, according to several sources.

Mahmoudian, who is a human rights defender and political journalist, was taken away by police agents from his home on Wednesday and charged with "anti-government propaganda." This came after he posted a warning on his Telegram channel that two protesters who have been jailed over the 2022 anti-government demonstrations sparked by the death of Mahsa Aminni — the 22-year-old Iranian Kurdish woman who died while in police custody for allegedly wearing a loose headscarf — were at risk of execution. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Record Store Day Co-Founder on How Black Friday Evolved Into a Major Holiday for Vinyl Hounds, and What Will Fly Off the Shelves This Year 'Adolescence' Breakout Owen Cooper Stars in New Beatles Music Video for 'In My Life'

Mahmoudian has previously served a five-year prison term between 2009 and 2014 on charges of “mutiny against the regime." He was also briefly arrested in February of this year, shortly before the Oscars, after signing a statement condemning Islamic Republic leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and the government's violent crackdown on demonstrators following mass anti-government protests in January.

The police agents who arrested Mahmoudian on Wednesday also seized his electronic devices, according to a post on his Telegram channel.

Mahmoudian is being held at the Greater Tehran Penitentiary, Europe-based Iranian activist Hosein Razzagh told the Associated Press on Thursday. His detention was also reported on Wednesday by reformist Iranian news outlet Emtedad.

News of his arrest follows recent reports that Panahi has been sentenced by a Tehran Revolutionary Court to five years and one month in jail, as well as the confiscation of his assets, the freezing of his bank accounts, and a two-year travel and social media ban. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Last week, the heads of Venice and Berlin film festivals as well as a slew of prominent actors and directors — including Mark Ruffalo, Tilda Swinton, Michael Moore, Barry Jenkins, Alex Gibney and many more — rallied to Panahi's defense in an open letter calling on the Tehran Revolutionary Court "to rescind all actions."

articles.summary: Max Marlow, who produced this year's Oscar-nominated short film "A Friend of Dorothy" starring Miriam Margolyes and Stephen Fry, is set to make his directorial debut. "Hidden Creatures" is a magical-realist short drama exploring invisible disability through what's described as an "unconventional coming-of-age story." Set in a cinema, the film follows 17-year-old Rafi on a […]
articles.content:
Max Marlow, who produced this year's Oscar-nominated short film " A Friend of Dorothy " starring Miriam Margolyes and Stephen Fry, is set to make his directorial debut.

"Hidden Creatures" is a magical-realist short drama exploring invisible disability through what's described as an "unconventional coming-of-age story."

Set in a cinema, the film follows 17-year-old Rafi on a date; nervous not because he's with a girl, but because of the creature he's hiding from her under his shirt. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories The Best Beatles Books, Vinyl and Merch to Gift Beatlemaniacs This Year Noah Kahan Deserved More Grammy Love Than Just One Minor Nomination. Here's Why He Didn't Get It

Newcomer Oliver Kaye will make his screen debut in the lead role, bringing personal lived experience to a character navigating the complexities of a situation that the filmmakers say remains largely unseen by those around him.

Kaye, known online to his 18K+ followers as @thekidwithabag, is a medical student and U.K. advocate for invisible illnesses, who shares his life living with a stoma bag following surgery to remove his large intestine due to ulcerative colitis in 2020. Marlow, having undergone the same surgery almost 10 years prior, was drawn to casting Kaye after an initial introduction through mutual family friends to offer advice led him to discover Ollie’s camera-facing social media presence.

"I see a lot of myself, in Rafi, particularly in the emotional and mental challenges of navigating life with a stoma and an invisible condition," says Marlow. “It was especially important to me that his story reflected the realities that so many people face and are often misunderstood.”

On his first time acting, Kaye said: “Making my screen debut brought a whole range of emotions, from nerves and the uncertainty of stepping into something completely new, to excitement at being part of a project, bigger than myself, with such an important and powerful message. I’m incredibly grateful to Max, the entire team and all the cast for supporting me throughout to draw on both the lived experiences I and people living with invisible illnesses have and the acting side of the role." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Also joining the cast is actor Adam Rhazali ("Shetland"), who plays James and brings his own lived experience of alopecia to the production. His casting reflects the film's wider commitment to authentic representation.

"After conversations with experts and others with similar lived experience, I knew authentic casting would be essential on this film, which at its core explores the parts of ourselves we hide to fit in with everyone else," said Marlow, who wrote the screenplay drawing on his own experiences.

"Having Ollie and Adam bring parts of their own lives to Rafi and James is something I don't take for granted. There's a vulnerability and understanding they bring to their characters that simply can't be manufactured. Although this is a story told through metaphor, I hope the experiences it represents feel recognisable and honest, and that the film opens up conversations that continue long after its festival run and wider release."

Behind the camera, "Hidden Creatures" marks the first film credit for Sir Stelios Haji-Ioannou, better known as the founder and former CEO of budget airline EasyJet, who serves as executive producer. The film is being produced by Marlow through his A Marlow's Production banner, in association with Blue Lobster Productions, the Nick Maughan Foundation, the Sandhu Charitable Foundation and the Stelios Philanthropic Foundation. Alongside Haji-Ioannou, executive producers are Jai Sandhu and Nick Maughan. Haji-Ioannou. Charities Alopecia UK and RAiISE have each expressed support for the project.

The short film completed principal photography at South London's Peckhamplex Cinema in November, shot on Kodak 35mm by BIFA-nominated cinematographer Jermaine Canute Edwards ("My Father's Shadow"). The film also features practical, Henson-inspired in-camera creature effects, with puppets designed and created by Andy Heath of Talk to the Hand Puppets.

"Hidden Creatures" is intended to premiere in 2027. Further casting announcements will follow.

articles.title: I Asked Marshals’ Logan Marshall-Green Why Cal Calls Kayce Coyote
articles.summary: I had a question; he had the answer.
articles.content:
At this point on Marshals, I never use Cal’s full name, Pete Calvin. His nickname is used far more than his full name, and now, Cal’s putting in the work to make sure his team has nicknames like him. For example, as Season 2 of Marshals has been airing on the 2026 TV schedule , I’ve noticed Cal calling Kayce Coyote a lot. So, with all this in mind, I asked Logan Marshall-Green, who plays Cal, what’s up with the nicknames, and specifically Kayce’s.

So, the backstory behind the nickname is unknown, at least to Logan Marshall-Green. However, it is something that’s important to Cal and Kayce’s shared history. If I had to guess, Kayce got the nickname while they were both SEALs, and it’s just stuck. I personally hope Cal is the one responsible for it, and maybe someday that can be addressed in the show.

So, we have Dre and Coyote. We have Dust Cloud too. However, Belle still does not have a nickname because it sounds like Kebbel vetoed it. Knowing Cal and Belle’s relationship, that feels hilariously fitting. However, I do hope that someday she can get a nickname too.

articles.title: 5 Forgotten 1990s Sci-fi Shows Every '80s Kid Owes It To Themselves to Rediscover
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of SkyDance The 1990s were the first decade of a new world. Historian Francis Fukuyama called it "the end of history" – something he's been continually clowned by people of younger generations who don't understand the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The 1990s were the first decade of a new world. The Cold War had ended in 1989, with the Soviet Union collapsing after years of trying to match the United States. Historian Francis Fukuyama called it "the end of history" – something he's been continually clowned by people of younger generations who don't understand the concept. Of course, it was also wrong – the world didn't find some utopian new balance where we shared wealth and success with everyone. It was a time of change, though; grunge destroyed hair metal, hip hop began its road to cultural dominance, and rave culture was bringing around a new kind of hippie. It felt like the world was getting weirder, especially when it came to pop culture.

Sci-fi has always been an important part of pop culture and the '90s would see a new rise of the genre. We were on the cusp of a new millennium and we were obsessed with the utopian new world we where going to create. Looking back, the '90s were such a naive time, but there was some fantastic sci-fi in the decade, especially on TV. Star Trek: The Next Generation was joined Deep Space Nine and Voyager , X-Files was making sci-fi cool again, and the prequels were coming down the road, but there was way more great sci-fi out there that has been all but forgotten. This '80s baby recommends these 5 forgotten '90s sci-fi shows, perfect shows to rediscover for the '80s kid who wants to remember a life without back pain.

Sci-fi and anime have gone together beautifully for decades, and the '90s has numerous examples of awesome sci-fi anime. There were classics like Neon Genesis Evangelion, Ghost in the Shell , five different Gundam series', and numerous others. I want to take you back in time to a random Sunday morning in the mid '90s. I ended up waking up at some ridiculous time, put on the TV, and saw an anime. It was a mech anime, about an amnesiac named Slade, who was found in space and brought to Earth, which was at war with a mysterious race of monsters. Slade had the power to transform into a mech, battling the aliens and the mysterious Blade with his Technoman form.

I was hooked to show – titled Technoman – but there was never season two. At least, not in the US. In Japan, the name of the show was Tekkaman Blade (they changed his name to Slade because Blade was more of a villain name in the US) and it went on to have several sequels and reboots over the years. Tekkaman Blade was fantastic; while it wasn't as deep as something like Evangelion or Gundam , it was still something completely different than anything on US TV at the time. The entire series is subbed in English on YouTube and it's definitely worth your time. It was so hard to be weeb in the '90s in the US unless you had money (you had to import everything and it was super expensive for the VHS sets), so it was nice to get something like Technoman .

The '80s were the decade of the Saturday morning cartoon, when the Reagan Administration changed the FCC rules on children's shows, allowing them to become toy commercials with no educational value (read that sentence again and think about why the world is the way it is). The '90s would see numerous new series drop, but one of the best is one that you probably don't remember: Exosquad . This sci-fi cartoon take place in a future where humanity is battling the Neosapiens of Mars in "exoframes", robotic war suits that link to the brains of their pilots, giving them immediate reaction time.

Exosquad was interesting in that it was probably one of the most mature American Saturday morning cartoons I ever watched. This wasn't like the war between Corbra and G.I. Joe, this was a serious conflict with the fate of two races at stake. It was dark and I loved it. The writers of the show didn't talk down to their audience and gave them a show that stands up even today. Honestly, this show has more in common with anime of the '90s than other American shows; it's basically an American mech anime. If that appeals to you, then go to Peacock and check this one out.

The '90s were a time when Hollywood was trying to create new pop culture franchises and sci-fi was always fertile ground for that sort of thing. Sci-fi fans are devoted to the genre in a different way than others and if a show can find a fanbase, they have a good chance of surviving. In 1994, James Spader and Kurt Douglas starred in Stargate , a movie where the titular gate takes them to space Egypt, where they learn the secrets of the pyramids and that alien exists and thing of that nature. I saw it in theaters and loved it, but the movie wasn't a massive success (can you believe it was the first place I saw James Spader?). However, three years later, the story would continue with the excellent Stargate SG-1 .

The show would have MacGuyver legend Richard Dean Anderson (suddenly I feel like Patty and Selma and I love it) replace Douglas and Michael Shanks take over for Spader. The primary cast was rounded out by Amanda Tapping and the excellent Christopher Judge (Teal'c was basically Worf if he didn't get jobbed out to blue barrels). The SG-1 team used the Stargate to protect the Earth and gain alien technology, battling the alien conquerors known as the Goa'uld. The show ran for ten years on three different networks – Showtime, the Sci-Fi Channel, and Sky1 – and had spinoffs like Stargate: Atlantis and Stargate Universe . It's a great show and it's about time everyone remembered that.

TV execs had learned by the '90s that if you gave a sci-fi show a chance to grow a little bit, it could have legs. X-Files showed that viewers were down for a little weirder sci-fi, so execs would give shows with out there premises more of a chance to grow than they would have. Sliders was one of these. The show began in 1995 and ran to the year 2000 and the quickest way to describe the show is that it was Quantum Leap with an ensemble and instead of traveling through time, they jumped from universe to universe.

Quinn Mallory, played by Jerry O'Connel, created a device that would allow him to "slide" through alternate universes, equipped with a timer that would allow him to return home. Quinn, Professor Arturo, Rembrandt, and Wade gave the machine a try, but the system was damaged and the only way for them to get home was to keep sliding through the universes until they hit theirs. The show ran for three seasons on Fox before finishing up its run on the Sci-Fi Channel with two seasons. This show was so much fun back in the day, and it's still amazing today.

'90s sci-fi was brilliant and one of the best examples of that is Babylon 5 . The show was created by writer/producer J. Michael Straczynski, who ended up writing 92 of the show's 110 episodes. That was unheard of back then and even more rare now, when showrunners rarely write anything but the first episode. The show told the story of the titular space station. One of five Babylon stations built, it was the only one that survived, with the first three being destroyed before they were finished, the fourth disappearing. The station became the epicenter of the galaxy's drama, as Earth, the Mimbari, the Narn, and the Centauri all bump against each other when a new threat rears its ugly head.

The 1990s were a decade where we had two different sci-fi shows set on space stations at the same time (there are rumors that Trek producers heard about JMS's pitch and made their own space station show), both of them seeing a coalition of galactic powers come together to battle a terrible new threat. However, they're also very different shows; Stracyznski show digs more into the fantastical side of sci-fi, and that's part of its charm. Babylon 5 was never as big as DS9, but it's just as brilliant in completely different ways.

What '90s sci-fi classic do you love the most? Any of them you would recommend? Sound off in the comment section below.
